- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. - general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. ## pencil
The Pencil MCP server is the editor for .pen design files (web/mobile apps and websites). Use it to read, generate, and validate designs.

.pen files are encrypted: access them only via "pencil" MCP tools — never use Read or Grep on .pen files. Follow each tool's input schema exactly.

Always call get_editor_state(include_schema: true) if you don't have the current .pen file schema in the context. Knowing the schema is required to use any other Pencil MCP tool.

Tools: get_editor_state, get_guidelines, batch_get, batch_design, snapshot_layout, get_screenshot, get_variables, export_nodes, export_html.

- code-review: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes — Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/PRD asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when the user wants to pin down domain terminology or a ubiquitous language, record an architectural decision, or when another skill needs to maintain the domain model.
- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
- resolving-merge-conflicts: Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict.
- tdd: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
- releases: CipherBox v2 release and staging-deploy mechanics — release-please layout, the two version surfaces, staging tag pipeline, and the v1 freeze. Use when cutting a release, deploying to staging, or touching release/versioning config.
- crypto-privacy-review: Review code for cryptographic security, generate test cases and edge cases
- resolve-pr-reviews: Resolve PR Review Comments
- ship: Ship
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.content:
#927 feat(web): ask the engine for the vault root instead of seeding an anchor
merged: 2026-08-01T09:05:56Z
---
## Problem

`apps/web/src/engine/snapshotStore.ts` seeded its first pull with a hardcoded
all-zero id16 (`VAULT_ROOT_SEED_ID`) because the wasm host exposed no way to ask
for "the vault root": `snapshot(folder: &NodeId)` required a folder id, and the
UI cannot name one before it has seen a view — the root only arrives inside
`SnapshotDescriptor.root`.

That seed was correct only by coincidence. Cold start replaces the whole base
snapshot, so an adopted base rooted at anything but the anchor made the very
first `snapshot()` reject with `UnknownNode` and painted a bare error where the
vault should be. `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs` already calls `view.root()` — the
desktop host asks. Now the web host asks too.

## Change

1. `crates/wasm/src/host.rs` — `snapshot(folder: Option<NodeId>)`, falling back
   to `Engine::root()` under the same read lock. No facade change, no new
   command, no new event.
2. `folder` widened to `Uint8Array | null` through the TS chain — signature-only
   edits in `protocol.ts`, `engineWasm.ts`, `engineHost.ts`, `transport.ts`,
   `correlatedTransport.ts`, `broadcast.ts`, `broadcastTransport.ts`,
   `facade.ts`, `engineClient.ts`, `testkit.ts`. `serve.ts` and `leaderRelay.ts`
   needed no edit — the widened type flows through them.
3. `VAULT_ROOT_SEED_ID` and the `state.view?.root` fallback chain are gone from
   `snapshotStore.ts`; it pulls with `focus` directly.

## Tests

- `packages/client/test/browser/engine.spec.ts` — the real WASM engine answers a
  rootless `snapshot(null)` from its own root. Reverting only the `host.rs`
  signature fails it with `EngineRequestError: expected instance of NodeId`.
- `apps/web/src/engine/snapshotStore.test.ts` — the unfocused pull names no
  folder at all, and a base rooted at a non-anchor id paints. Against the seeded
  constant it failed with `expected Uint8Array[ 0, 0, 0, … ] to be null`.
- `packages/client/src/broadcastTransport.test.ts` — `null` survives the
  cross-tab structured clone, so a follower's rootless read reaches the leader as
  no folder at all.

## Verification

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo check -p cipherbox-wasm --target
wasm32-unknown-unknown --all-targets`, `pnpm -r --if-present run typecheck`,
`pnpm -r --if-present run test`, `eslint .`, and the full browser suite
`pnpm --filter @cipherbox/client test:browser` (19 passed) — all exit 0.

Closes #900


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Snapshot requests can now omit a folder to automatically use the vault’s root.
  * Root-level snapshots are consistently supported across local, browser, worker, and broadcast operations.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved initial snapshot handling for vaults with adopted roots.
  * Prevented errors caused by incorrect or unavailable root identifiers.
* **Tests**
  * Added coverage validating rootless snapshots and root propagation.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

### Cross-cutting requirement — bound content-fetch peak memory in the JS `HttpSeam` (from #742/#787, closed engine-side by #783)
The engine caps fetched content-block size at the fetch boundary (`MAX_RESOLVED_RECORD_BYTES` = 4 MiB). Desktop enforces a **true streaming peak-memory bound** (Content-Length pre-check + a chunked read that aborts once accumulated bytes exceed the cap). The browser JS `HttpSeam` (`packages/client/src/seams/http.ts`) must do the same when the engine worker fetches content: enforce a `maxBytes` limit while draining `Response.body` via a `ReadableStream` reader, aborting past the cap — instead of materializing the full body first. Today it does only a `Content-Length` pre-check, so a gateway that omits or lies about `Content-Length` can still force a full-body buffer in the tab (a browser-tab OOM). Main is clean, no open PRs, and #927 closed #900. Here's the state.

## The unblock that #927 bought

**#805** (harvest the v1 vault browser read path) had three deps: #803 ✅, #900 ✅ (just now), **#917** ❌. That's the only thing standing between you and the whole web read path.

**#917** — "nothing resolves a folder record below the scope root on a device that did not author it" — has **zero dependencies** ("`ChildAdopter`, `resolve`, `project_folder`, `focus_set` all exist today"). It is now the single critical-path item in the repo.

```
#917 → #805 → #806 (folder CRUD)
             → #807 (download/preview, #802 ✅)
             → #808 (staleness/offline chrome)
             → #914 (auth from engine)
             → #809 (web e2e smoke gate) → #913
```

## Ready to start right now, in parallel

**Web** (independent of #917):
- **#910** — SIWE below the facade. Shares the facade-threading surface with #914 (`protocol.ts`/transports/`facade.ts`); land one, rebase the other. #910 first, since #914 also wants #805.
- **#641** — SW byte pipe + app-shell precache. Deps clear, and it carries the cross-cutting residual: streaming `maxBytes` bound in the JS `HttpSeam` (today only a `Content-Length` pre-check → tab OOM on a lying gateway).
- **#888** — CSP + nosniff on the staging vhost. Small; #882 landed in #889.
- **#836** — browser mailbox seam speaks a protocol the API never served. Deps: none, #827 landed.
- **#873** — file upload through facade write handles. Its stated blockers #868 and #896 are **both closed now** — this is quietly unblocked, though practically it wants #805's browser first.

**Engine write plane** (all dep-clear):
- #920, #921 — both gated on #916, which landed.
- #869, #924, #926, #918, #909, #860, #871, #872 — no listed deps.
- #915 — engine-side ceiling change was writable already; its contract gate needed #906, which landed in #912. Fully unblocked.
- #933 — Authorization-header consolidation, trivial.

**Settings chain** is strictly serial and #928 just landed: **#929 → #930 → #931**. #930 is a decision issue (cold-device freshness anchor) — #931 only exists under two of its three options, so #930 could delete #931.

**Core**: #936 and #937 are the follow-on from #935 (the wipe/redact work), no other deps.

## Recommendation

Start **#917** now — nothing else in the tree unblocks as much, and it's engine-local. Run **#910** and **#641** alongside it on the web side, since neither touches #917's surface. The write-plane engine cluster (#920/#921/#869/#924) is a good third lane if you want a wider fan-out.

One bit of hygiene: #900 is closed but its tracker checkbox in #655 is still unticked (same for #916's downstream framing). Want me to sweep the tracker checkboxes against actual issue state?

You are auditing GitHub issue dependency hygiene in the repo at /Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box (FSM1/cipher-box). READ-ONLY on the working tree — do not edit any files, do not create branches. You may edit GitHub issue bodies (see "Fixes" below).

ALWAYS prefix gh with `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN` (e.g. `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh issue view 920`).

## Context

This repo runs a v2 build tracked by umbrella issue #655 ("v2 build tracker"), milestone v2.0.0, label `v2-build`. The house convention for every issue filed as a follow-up out of a PR review is:

1. The issue body contains a `## Depends on` section naming its hard blockers by number (or explicitly "None" / "Nothing" with a justification).
2. The dependency edge is BIDIRECTIONAL — the blocker issue should also say what it blocks, or the relationship must at least be discoverable from both ends. A deferred issue filed with no dependency edge orphans and is never scheduled; that is the failure mode we are hunting.
3. The issue carries `Part of #655` (or is listed as a child of a nearer umbrella like #904 or #642) AND appears as a checkbox line in the #655 tracker body.
4. It carries the `v2-build` label, an appropriate `comp:*` label, and the `v2.0.0` milestone where applicable.

## Task

Scope: every issue CREATED in roughly the last 3 weeks (use `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh issue list --state all --limit 200 --json number,title,state,createdAt,labels,milestone --jq '...'` and filter by createdAt >= 2026-07-10). These came out of recent PR review sweeps. Today's date is 2026-08-01.

For EACH such issue (open and closed — closed ones matter less, note but don't fix them):

- Fetch the body. Extract the `## Depends on` section (and any "Blocked by" / "Depends on" prose elsewhere in the body).
- Resolve every issue number it names: does that issue exist, is it OPEN or CLOSED? A dependency on a CLOSED issue means the item is unblocked — flag any issue whose stated blockers are all closed but which is still described as blocked (these are silently-ready work).
- Check the reverse edge: does the named blocker's body (or the tracker #655) reflect the relationship? Flag missing reverse edges.
- Check it is listed in the #655 tracker body. Flag any issue that is NOT listed anywhere in the tracker — that is an orphan.
- Check labels + milestone against the convention above.
- Flag issues with NO dependency statement at all (neither a `## Depends on` section nor an explicit "None") — the primary defect class.
- Also flag tracker checkbox drift: issues that are CLOSED but still show `- [ ]` in the #655 body, or open ones showing `- [x]`.

## Fixes you may apply

Apply ONLY unambiguous, mechanical fixes:
- Adding a missing `v2-build` label, `comp:*` label, or `v2.0.0` milestone that clearly matches the issue's subject area (match the pattern of its siblings).
- Adding a missing `Part of #655` line to a body that has none.

Do NOT invent dependency edges, do NOT edit the #655 tracker body, and do NOT close anything. Anything requiring judgement about what blocks what → report it as a recommendation with your proposed edge and the evidence for it, and leave the issue alone.

When editing an issue body, fetch the current body to a file, edit the file, and patch with `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh issue edit <N> --body-file <file>` so you never lose content. Use the scratchpad dir /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-myankelev-Code-random-cipher-box/d6d4959d-7e94-4b31-b5a4-2baeac1e123c/scratchpad for temp files.

## Report

Return a compact structured report (this is a return value, not a chat message):

1. **Orphans** — issues with no dependency statement and/or absent from the tracker. Number, title, what's missing.
2. **Silently ready** — issues whose stated blockers have all closed. Number, title, blockers and when they closed.
3. **Missing reverse edges** — pairs, with the proposed edge text.
4. **Tracker checkbox drift** — closed-but-unticked and open-but-ticked lines in #655.
5. **Label/milestone gaps** — what you fixed, what you left.
6. **Fixes applied** — exact list of issue numbers and what changed.

Be precise with issue numbers. Do not pad the report with narrative.

## 0. Setup

- You are in a dedicated git worktree forked from `main` at `afb388752`. Other agents are working sibling issues in their own worktrees concurrently.
- Confirm where you are: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and `git branch --show-current`.
- Record your own fork base: `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` — verify it is `afb388752` before starting. Do not trust any reported worktree metadata over this.
- Branch: `git checkout -b <type>/<issue-number>-<short-slug>` (types: feat/fix/refactor/test/chore/docs/perf/ci/build/style).
- Run `pnpm install` in the worktree. Do NOT symlink `node_modules` from the main checkout — it breaks.

## 1. Recon (mandatory)

- Read `AGENTS.md` and `CONTEXT.md` at the repo root, plus the `blueprint/*.md` that governs your slice. The blueprint corpus is normative; `docs/` is v1 legacy and is NOT.
- Check branch `v1` for a reference implementation of the surface you are touching: `git log v1 --oneline -- <path>`, `git show v1:<path>`. This recon is mandatory before scoping any v2 surface — v1 has repeatedly overturned assumptions made without it. `v1` is frozen: read it, never change it.
- Read the issues your issue links before designing.

## 2. Implement

- Use the v2 ubiquitous language from `CONTEXT.md` exactly.
- All crypto/codec/engine logic is Rust (`crates/core`, `crates/engine`). TypeScript never implements crypto; TS exists only in `packages/client` and `apps/web`.
- Determinism is injected: entropy, time, and policy arrive as parameters or seam traits. Never call a clock or RNG directly in core/engine logic.
- Prefer TS string-literal unions over TS enums.
- v2 is greenfield: NO backward compatibility, no migration arms, no `serde(default)` compat shims.
- Encode/decode fail-closed symmetry: if a decode path hard-rejects an invariant, the matching encode path must enforce it with a RELEASE-ACTIVE check returning `Err` — never `debug_assert!`/`assert!`, which are stripped in release. Cover it with a test that fires in a release build. This is a recurring P1 finding; follow the `crates/core/src/seal/body.rs` `assert_children_unique` convention.
- Zeroize at the terminal owner only — a callee must not zero a caller-owned or reused buffer.
- Comments explain WHY, and stay short. No absence-justifying comments (prose about paths that are not in the code). No apologia for workarounds — if it needs a paragraph to defend it, fix the code instead. No doc blocks defending code your diff does not change.
- Every suite must block a merge in a named CI gate the day it lands. Assert behavior, never source text.
- Implement small in-scope things now rather than deferring. If you genuinely must defer, `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh issue create`, label `v2-build`, give it an immediate bidirectional depends-on edge, and add `Part of #655`.

## 3. Verify — every one must exit 0

- `cargo fmt --all` (NEVER scope with `-p`; the CI gate is `cargo fmt --all --check`)
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`
- If you touched `crates/wasm` or any seam trait bound: `cargo check -p cipherbox-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --all-targets`. `--workspace` never builds wasm32, so nothing else catches it.
- `cargo test` for the crates you touched
- `pnpm -r --if-present run typecheck`, `pnpm -r --if-present run test`, `eslint .`
- If you touched `packages/client` browser surfaces: `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/client test:browser`
- `apps/web` vitest only collects `*.test.ts` — a `.spec.ts` is silently skipped. Web unit tests are also excluded from the main CI Test job, so hoist logic worth testing into a package that IS gated.
- Rebuild dependent dists before consumer typechecks if you changed a package API.

## 4. Review gates (mandatory, on your own diff `git diff main...HEAD`)

- `/security-review` — trust boundaries, fail-closed behavior, auth/expiry gates, injection, DoS/resource exhaustion, concurrency, determinism seams.
- `/simplify` — speculative generality, dead abstraction, duplication.
- `/crypto-privacy-review` — REQUIRED if the diff touches crypto: `crates/core` primitives, key/seal material, or trust-boundary/fail-closed reads.

Invoke via the Skill tool. If a skill is unavailable in your environment, do a rigorous manual pass against that checklist instead — never skip a gate. Fold real findings back into code and tests.

## 5. Commit

- Conventional Commits: `type(scope): description`, imperative mood. NO parenthesized text in the subject line — it breaks Release Please parsing and CI rejects the PR title.
- Commit signing goes through the 1Password SSH agent and can hang: run `git commit` via a background, UNSANDBOXED Bash call with a `timeout` guard. Never pass `--no-gpg-sign`. If a helper reports failure, check `git log` before retrying — it frequently landed anyway.
- markdownlint runs on staged `.md`: no `**bold**` as a heading (use `###`), blank lines around fences and lists.

## 6. PR

- Push your branch. NEVER push to `main`.
- `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh pr create --draft --base main`. Body covers: Problem, Change, Tests (including which test fails when you revert the fix), Verification (the exact commands above and their results), and `Closes #<your issue>`.
- Keep it a DRAFT. Do not mark it ready — the user controls CodeRabbit timing.
- No Claude attribution, no session link, no "Generated with" footer, in either the PR body or a commit trailer.
- Do not escape real issue references like `#916`; DO escape non-issue `#NN` (a line number, say). Cross-repo refs are `FSM1/cipher-box-next#NN`.
- `gh pr edit` fails against this repo's classic Projects — patch a body with `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.
- Creating a PR triggers a bot `chore(release)` push, so any later push needs `git fetch` + rebase first.

## 7. Report back

Return: branch name, PR number and URL, a 3-6 line summary of the change, which verification commands ran and their results, what the review gates found and how you resolved each, and anything you deferred with the issue number you filed. If you got blocked, say exactly where and why — never report success for partial work.

fn registered_content_cids(device: &FakeDevice, name: &IpnsName) -> Vec<String> {

        .requests()
        .iter()
        .filter(|request| request.url.ends_with("/registry/register"))

                    .as_array()?
                    .iter()
                    .filter_map(|cid| cid.as_str().map(str::to_owned))
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>(),

        })
        .next_back()
        .unwrap_or_default()

/// The `contentCids` the device's last registration for `name` carried — what a
/// sub-EOL renewal will re-pin (#797).
fn registered_content_cids(device: &FakeDevice, name: &IpnsName) -> Vec<String> {
    device
        .http
        .requests()
        .iter()
        .filter(|request| request.url.ends_with("/registry/register"))
        .filter_map(|request| {
            serde_json::from_slice::<serde_json::Value>(request.body.as_deref()?).ok()
        })
        .filter_map(|body| body.as_array()?.first().cloned())
        .filter(|entry| entry["ipnsName"] == name.as_str())
        .filter_map(|entry| {

                    .as_array()?
                    .iter()
                    .filter_map(|cid| cid.as_str().map(str::to_owned))
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            )
        })
        .next_back()
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

**Files (all `apps/web`, nothing in `packages/sdk` or `packages/sdk-core`):**

  - `apps/web/src/hooks/useDropUpload.ts` — the orchestrator.
  - `apps/web/src/services/upload.service.ts` + `packages/sdk-core/src/ipfs/index.ts` — thread an axios `CancelToken` into `addToIpfs`.

**Semantics:**
- Cancel is owned by the **web store**, not the SDK. It uses legacy **axios `CancelToken`** (deprecated), not `AbortController`/`AbortSignal`. No `AbortSignal` anywhere in the upload path.
- `cancelFile` fires `cancelSource.cancel('Upload cancelled by user')` and **immediately `next.delete(id)`** — the row disappears from the store with no terminal `cancelled` status. There is no state machine and no point-of-no-return check; cancel is never refused.
- **Critical gap:** `client.uploadFiles(...)` (`packages/sdk/src/client.ts:1203`) takes **no cancel token / signal** — only `callbacks` and `{encryptFn, pinFn}`. So for the primary new-file batch path, cancel is *cosmetic*: it removes the UI row, and encryption + pin continue to completion server-side. The token is only actually honored on the **duplicate/replace** path, where `useDropUpload.ts:224` pulls `cancelSource.token` and passes it to `addToIpfs`.
- Cancel is only checked at coarse boundaries: `useDropUpload.ts:129-131` (entry missing → skip before file read) and `:211` (throw `'Upload cancelled by user'` before duplicate encrypt). Sentinel-string comparison, not a typed error — `upload.service.ts:34-35` also uses the string to suppress retry.
- Store is keyed per-file (`Map<id, PerFileUpload>`), but the batch is one SDK call, so per-file abort of an in-flight slot is not expressible.

## 2. Orphan / GC — three unrelated, partial mechanisms; no unified staged-block GC

- **Web, best-effort, in-memory only:** `useDropUpload.ts:110/231/262-270` tracks `orphanCids[]` (only the duplicate-staged CIDs) and fires `unpinFromIpfs` in the catch block. Fire-and-forget, no persistence — a tab close or crash leaks. `ReplaceFileDialog.tsx:53-79` does the same on skip/skip-all/failure. Note: CIDs from the **SDK batch path are never tracked**, so a mid-batch failure leaks pins.
- **API, read-only drift report:** `apps/api/src/ipfs/pending-unpin/pending-unpin.processor.ts` — `runDriftReport()` diffs Kubo `pin/ls?type=recursive` against `pinned_cids ∪ pending_unpins` and only **logs + increments `cipherbox_drift_orphaned_pins_total`**. Comment at D-06 is explicit: "never deletes anything." Actual deletion is refcount-driven via the `pending_unpins` outbox (`drainPendingUnpins`/`refcountAndMaybeUnpin` under `withCidLock`), not reachability/GC.
- **Desktop Rust, the only real GC:** `crates/sdk/src/queue.rs:480 gc_failed_entries(age_days, total_size_budget)` — three passes over the journal dir: age purge, size purge (oldest-first), and orphan `.bin` sidecar cleanup where liveness = "sibling `.json` parsed successfully". Explicitly **only touches `Failed` entries; `Pending`/`InProgress` are never GC'd**. Invoked once at mount (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/mod.rs:204`, `fuse/windows/mod.rs:116`), best-effort, non-fatal; no background scheduler.

## Things that would overturn a v2 assumption

1. Do **not** assume the SDK has a cancellable upload to build on — `uploadFiles`/`uploadFile` have no signal parameter at all. Adding `AbortSignal` is greenfield in `packages/sdk`, not a port.
2. v1 has **no `cancelled` terminal state** — the row is deleted. If v2 wants "cancelled" distinct from "error"/"dismissed", there is no prior art.
3. v1 has **no point-of-no-return concept**. Cancel after the pin succeeds but before folder publish is simply unhandled; the CID leaks (only the duplicate path registers it in `orphanCids`).
4. Server-side orphan handling is deliberately **detect-only**, refcount-based. A v2 design that assumes a server GC will reclaim cancelled blocks would be assuming a mechanism that does not exist on v1 — the drift counter is an alerting signal, and BYO advisory rows in `pinned_cids` intentionally count as "accounted" (IN-05/WR-07), so reachability-based GC would conflict with that refcount model.
5. The only durable, crash-safe cleanup model in the repo is the desktop journal (`Failed`-only, age+size budget, mount-time sweep) — that is the closest thing to a GC design precedent, and it deliberately refuses to touch in-flight work.</result>

<result>## Security review — #924 mark-before-release (branch `fix/924-mark-before-release`)

**No high-confidence findings. The change is sound and strictly narrows the failure surface.** Full test suite passes (`cargo test -p cipherbox-engine --test write_plane`: 47/47, including the pre-existing fail-closed guards `an_evicted_prefix_of_the_block_set_is_loss_not_progress` and `a_hole_in_the_staged_block_suffix_is_loss_and_fails_closed`).

Reasoning that rules out each candidate:

**1. Can the mark now claim un-uploaded bytes?** No. Both orderings write the mark strictly *after* `upload_block` returned `Ok`, i.e. after a confirmed `UploadResult` (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:1354`, `:1460`). The diff moves the mark only relative to `remove_staged_bytes`, never relative to the upload. The predicate "mark ⇒ these bytes were acked by the pin store" is byte-identical before and after. Failure paths between the two statements: `mark_uploaded` failing → `map_err(seam)` → `Halt::Unclassified` (`:1873`), which `apply_valve` (`:494`) treats as a no-op — the op keeps its queue place and its staged bytes, no attempt charge, no dead-letter, so a persistently failing mark write can never destroy a version. `remove_staged_bytes` failing after a successful mark → same `Halt::Unclassified`, leaf stays staged and marked, next pass re-uploads and re-removes. Process death between the two is the same state. A pin store that acks without persisting is a pre-existing trust assumption of `upload_block`, unchanged by the diff.

**2. Is the "still-staged blocks are a suffix" invariant intact?** Yes. At any interruption point the staged leaf set is `{i, i+1, …}` for some suffix start `s`; the only change is that `uploaded` may now be `s+1` instead of exactly `s` (the marked-but-not-yet-released leaf). Checking every reader:
- Hole guard `None if index >= uploaded` (`drain.rs:1364`): absent leaves have `index ≤ s-1 < s ≤ uploaded`, so it still never fires on legitimate progress, and it still fires on a genuine evicted prefix/hole (the two guard tests confirm). The one-index widening (`uploaded = s+1` skipping an absent leaf at index `s`) is sound precisely because that mark was written after that leaf's confirmed upload — the bytes are on the network.
- `orphan_staging_keys` (`crates/engine/src/sync/staging.rs:63-98`): expands leaves through the still-staged root, so a marked-and-staged residue leaf is *referenced*, never collected. `UPLOAD_MARK_KEY` is in the referenced set (`staging.rs:72`). The "a root whose bytes are gone is a finished upload" shortcut (`staging.rs:83`) concerns the root, which is released only in `release_staged_blocks` after publish — untouched.
- `release_staged_blocks` (`drain.rs:1481`) and `registered_by` (`drain.rs:1760`) both enumerate from the manifest, order-independent; a leaf that is still staged is simply removed/registered as normal.

**3. Can the marked-AND-staged residue be misread?** The only readers of `staged_keys()` in engine code are `orphan_staging_keys` (covered above) and the budget's `staged` total. The residue inflates the staged total for at most one pass, and `StagingLedger::admit` (`crates/engine/src/content/budget.rs:119-123`) uses it conservatively — it can refuse early, never over-admit. The `Some` arm re-uploads and re-removes it on the next pass, so it is transient. Only one such leaf can exist at a time, since a removal failure halts the pass.

**4. Mark scoping.** `upload_mark` (`drain.rs:1402-1417`) reads 0 unless the stored prefix equals this version's `root_cid`, so a mark from another version/op cannot advance this one's skip point. The mark is never cleared, only overwritten — but a stale mark for root A applied to a later version with root A is still sound: leaves are content-addressed, so the mark's claim ("these leaf CIDs are pinned") remains true for identical bytes, and any leaf actually present in staging takes the `Some` arm and is re-uploaded regardless of the mark. The single global mark key clobbering across concurrent identities is pre-existing (unchanged by this diff) and fails in the conservative direction (mismatch → 0).

**5. Malicious/corrupt staging store.** A store that fabricates `UPLOAD_MARK_KEY` can make the drain skip leaves and publish an unreadable manifest — but that is the pre-existing trust the mark mechanism already places in host storage, identical in both orderings (the mark's *contents* are the same; only the durable interleaving with the removal moved). Design notes worth relaying:
- **`revoke` takes only the URL `register` returned** (via `ticketFromPath`); it does not also accept a bare ticket.
- **The broker holds one port at a time** — `serve()` detaches the previous port's listener and drops its cursors, which is what makes service-side re-brokering leak-free. Failure to advance is guarded: the cursor advances by the *requested* length, and every post-await step re-checks `streams.get(id) === cursor` so a `close` or a superseding `serve` during a read is a silent drop, never a stray chunk.
- **Degradation is observable** via `get streaming()`, false when the container is absent, `register` rejects, or no worker is available to take the offer.

Design notes worth relaying:
- **`revoke` takes only the URL `register` returned** (via `ticketFromPath`); it does not also accept a bare ticket.
- **The broker holds one port at a time** — `serve()` detaches the previous port's listener and drops its cursors, which is what makes service-side re-brokering leak-free. Failure to advance is guarded: the cursor advances by the *requested* length, and every post-await step re-checks `streams.get(id) === cursor` so a `close` or a superseding `serve` during a read is a silent drop, never a stray chunk.
- **Degradation is observable** via `get streaming()`, false when the container is absent, `register` rejects, or no worker is available to take the offer.

## Findings

### [LOW] A focus folder that never gate-passes is re-probed on every navigation, with no backoff

**Location:** `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:880-892` (`stamp_focus_refreshed`), `facade.rs:1786-1812` (`refresh_focus_on_access`)

Only folders in `report.refreshed` get stamped, so any folder that fails to merge — offline, a foreign scope, a poisoned record, a kind transplant — keeps its old stamp and stays permanently "due". Every subsequent `Command::SetFocus` therefore re-runs a full fan-out GET across the whole endpoint set for that folder, unthrottled. The comment at `facade.rs:882-884` states this as intent, and for the transient-offline case it is right; the problem is the permanent cases. A host that issues `SetFocus` per navigation (or per FUSE `readdir`) while a chain folder is persistently unresolvable turns each user keystroke into an endpoint fan-out, and an attacker who can serve one poisoned record at a focused name gets the client to re-fetch it forever.

**Impact:** traffic amplification proportional to host navigation rate; also amplifies the navigation-timing signal in the note below. No trust impact — the record still never renders.

**Recommendation:** track attempts separately from merges, e.g. stamp a `last_attempted` alongside `refreshed` and gate the on-access re-probe on `max(last_refreshed, last_attempted)`, or apply a short failure backoff. Keep the tick leg unthrottled so recovery is still automatic.

### [LOW] A child-gate trust violation on a focused folder is completely silent

**Location:** `crates/engine/src/net/focus.rs:113` (`ResolveOutcome::TrustViolation(_) => return None`), `focus.rs:79` (kind transplant `continue`)

Both arms discard the rejection with no event, no error, and no `blocked` state; `Command::SetFocus` returns `Ok(None)` regardless. From the host's side a poisoned or transplanted folder record is indistinguishable from "offline". That is exactly the staleness/trust-violation conflation project rule 6 warns against — the behavior is correctly fail-closed, but it is unobservable.

The root leg has the identical gap, explicitly deferred at `facade.rs:1556-1558` ("surfacing: #796"). This is not a regression, but the diff widens the surface #796 has to cover from one record to the whole focus chain.

**Recommendation:** no code change in this PR; add the child-gate focus path to the #796 surfacing scope so the deferral stays accurate.

### [LOW] The focus pass serializes O(depth) resolves ahead of the drain on every tick

**Location:** `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1591-1611` (focus block sits between the root resolve and the drain), `crates/engine/src/net/focus.rs:67-92` (sequential `for` loop)

`fanout_get_verify` waits for *every* endpoint to settle before picking the freshest copy, and `run` awaits one folder at a time. So a tick now costs `1 + chain_depth` serialized worst-case-endpoint round trips, and all of it lands before `Drain::run`. With a deep open folder and one slow/blackholed endpoint, publishing queued user ops is delayed by the full focus latency. The blueprint does specify "the open folder, its full ancestor chain to root", so the target set is right; only the serialization and the ordering are a choice.

**Impact:** availability/latency only — queued writes stall behind unrelated read reconciliation.

**Recommendation:** resolve the chain concurrently (the names are independent, and the pass already tolerates per-folder failure), or run the drain before the focus pass. This is more a `/security-review` DoS/resource item than a crypto one; flagging it here because the diff introduced it.

`refresh_focus_on_access` fires immediately on `Command::SetFocus`, unjittered, in deterministic nearest-first order. An observer at the accelerator or the public delegated-routing endpoints learns *that the user navigated at time T*, the depth of the chain, and the ordered set of IPNS names on the path — and those names are stable, long-lived per-folder public keys, so they are durable pseudonymous identifiers. The poll leg gets `jittered_cadence` for herd spread; the on-access leg does not.

The staleness threshold is a real damper (proved by `navigation_re_resolves_a_folder_only_past_the_staleness_threshold`), and navigation-as-trigger is explicitly the design (blueprint/engine.md "Sync core", #33 D2), so I do not think this needs a fix. `focus_folders` returns nearest-first, so a deep folder's children are projected before its parent's body has been consulted. If the parent no longer lists that folder, the parent's `departed` handling calls `remove_node` (`sync/project.rs:69-74`), which drops links but leaves the grandchildren's `NodeMeta` in `snapshot.nodes` as unlinked orphans. I chased the one window that could produce a base-vs-floor skew — a local publish moving `record_sequence` ahead of the durable floor — and it does not exist: `Drain::publish_node` self-adopts through `ChildAdopter::adopt` (`sync/drain.rs:1599-1615`), which advances the sequence floor *and* writes the snapshot cache (`net/resolve.rs:202`) before the base is repainted. So floor, cache, and base move in lockstep, and a stale cache below the floor is rejected rather than projected.
- **No floor advances from this path.** `open_at_floor` never calls an advance. The only advance the focus pass can trigger is `floor::advance_sequence_on_unseal` inside `ChildAdopter::adopt` (`net/child.rs:217`) — sequence floor only, after the AAD-confirmed unseal, never the scope read-epoch floor. **Read-seed handling — correct terminal-owner zeroization.** `FolderRefresh.scope_read_seed: &'a Zeroizing<[u8;32]>` (`focus.rs:53`) borrows; the caller owns. Each `ChildAdopter` takes a `.clone()` and terminally owns it, zeroizing on drop — and the adopter is constructed and dropped inside `adopt()`, so at most one clone is live at a time even for a deep chain. No callee zeroes a caller-owned buffer (project rule 7). Both call sites own their `Zeroizing` for exactly one pass: `facade.rs:1586` (the tick clone, later moved into the drain, dropped at iteration end) and `facade.rs:1808` (dropped at fn end). The seed never reaches the facade surface: `FolderRefreshReport` is `Vec<NodeId>` + `bool` (`focus.rs:29-37`), and no `Event` carries it. `RefCell` borrows around the seed map are statement-scoped and never span an `.await`.

Direction is right.

**Determinism.** `focus.rs` reads no clock and no RNG (the doc claim at `focus.rs:30-32` is accurate); `now` is a parameter to `stamp_focus_refreshed`, supplied by `scheduler.now()` in the tick and by `authored_at` (itself `self.seams.scheduler.now()`, `facade.rs:1697`) on the command path. **Error strings.** The pass emits none — every failure is a silent `continue`/`None`. No key material, no plaintext, nothing derived from a seed anywhere in the diff.

**Encode/decode fail-closed symmetry (rule 8).** The one new decode-side hard reject is the kind transplant at `focus.rs:71-80` (child ref says folder, sealed body is a file). This is presentation-layer only — a miss would cost a repaint, never a trust decision.

## Findings

### [LOW] A focus folder that never gate-passes is re-probed on every navigation, with no backoff

**Location:** `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:880-892` (`stamp_focus_refreshed`), `facade.rs:1786-1812` (`refresh_focus_on_access`)

Only folders in `report.refreshed` get stamped, so any folder that fails to merge — offline, a foreign scope, a poisoned record, a kind transplant — keeps its old stamp and stays permanently "due". Every subsequent `Command::SetFocus` therefore re-runs a full fan-out GET across the whole endpoint set for that folder, unthrottled. The comment at `facade.rs:882-884` states this as intent, and for the transient-offline case it is right; the problem is the permanent cases. A host that issues `SetFocus` per navigation (or per FUSE `readdir`) while a chain folder is persistently unresolvable turns each user keystroke into an endpoint fan-out, and an attacker who can serve one poisoned record at a focused name gets the client to re-fetch it forever.

**Impact:** traffic amplification proportional to host navigation rate; also amplifies the navigation-timing signal in the note below. No trust impact — the record still never renders.

**Recommendation:** track attempts separately from merges, e.g. stamp a `last_attempted` alongside `refreshed` and gate the on-access re-probe on `max(last_refreshed, last_attempted)`, or apply a short failure backoff. Keep the tick leg unthrottled so recovery is still automatic.

### [LOW] A child-gate trust violation on a focused folder is completely silent

**Location:** `crates/engine/src/net/focus.rs:113` (`ResolveOutcome::TrustViolation(_) => return None`), `focus.rs:79` (kind transplant `continue`)

Both arms discard the rejection with no event, no error, and no `blocked` state; `Command::SetFocus` returns `Ok(None)` regardless. From the host's side a poisoned or transplanted folder record is indistinguishable from "offline". That is exactly the staleness/trust-violation conflation project rule 6 warns against — the behavior is correctly fail-closed, but it is unobservable.

The root leg has the identical gap, explicitly deferred at `facade.rs:1556-1558` ("surfacing: #796"). This is not a regression, but the diff widens the surface #796 has to cover from one record to the whole focus chain.

**Recommendation:** no code change in this PR; add the child-gate focus path to the #796 surfacing scope so the deferral stays accurate.

### [LOW] The focus pass serializes O(depth) resolves ahead of the drain on every tick

**Location:** `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1591-1611` (focus block sits between the root resolve and the drain), `crates/engine/src/net/focus.rs:67-92` (sequential `for` loop)

`fanout_get_verify` waits for *every* endpoint to settle before picking the freshest copy, and `run` awaits one folder at a time. So a tick now costs `1 + chain_depth` serialized worst-case-endpoint round trips, and all of it lands before `Drain::run`. With a deep open folder and one slow/blackholed endpoint, publishing queued user ops is delayed by the full focus latency. The blueprint does specify "the open folder, its full ancestor chain to root", so the target set is right; only the serialization and the ordering are a choice.

**Impact:** availability/latency only — queued writes stall behind unrelated read reconciliation.

**Recommendation:** resolve the chain concurrently (the names are independent, and the pass already tolerates per-folder failure), or run the drain before the focus pass. This is more a `/security-review` DoS/resource item than a crypto one; flagging it here because the diff introduced it.

### [INFO] Navigation-timed probes are a stronger observer signal than poll-cadence probes

`refresh_focus_on_access` fires immediately on `Command::SetFocus`, unjittered, in deterministic nearest-first order. An observer at the accelerator or the public delegated-routing endpoints learns *that the user navigated at time T*, the depth of the chain, and the ordered set of IPNS names on the path — and those names are stable, long-lived per-folder public keys, so they are durable pseudonymous identifiers. The poll leg gets `jittered_cadence` for herd spread; the on-access leg does not.

The staleness threshold is a real damper (proved by `navigation_re_resolves_a_folder_only_past_the_staleness_threshold`), and navigation-as-trigger is explicitly the design (blueprint/engine.md "Sync core", #33 D2), so I do not think this needs a fix. Recording it so the trade is on the record rather than implicit.

### [INFO] Nearest-first projection order can leave orphan `NodeMeta` entries

`focus_folders` returns nearest-first, so a deep folder's children are projected before its parent's body has been consulted. If the parent no longer lists that folder, the parent's `departed` handling calls `remove_node` (`sync/project.rs:69-74`), which drops links but leaves the grandchildren's `NodeMeta` in `snapshot.nodes` as unlinked orphans. They cannot render (`children()` is link-driven), and any real re-link rebuilds the meta from the `ChildRef` — but a resurrected node inherits the orphan's stale `record_sequence`, which feeds the conditional-delete rebase rule (`sync/rebase.rs:344-349`). Extremely narrow and largely pre-existing; projecting root-ward first (reverse the vec) would close it for free.

<result>I have everything I need. Here are the efficiency findings, ranked by real payoff.

## Findings — EFFICIENCY (`/simplify`)

### 1. Every 1 MiB media window re-runs the full gated child resolve (IPNS record fetch + sealed-body block fetch + unseal)
`/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-adea2eb962539584b/crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2152` (`read_content_range` → `head_version`), driven per-window from `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-adea2eb962539584b/packages/client/src/media/broker.ts:136`.

`head_version` (facade.rs:2186) does base-snapshot lookup → `resolve(record_transport, snapshot_cache, adopter, &name)` → `adopter.open_at_floor` → `assemble_envelope` (fetches the head block over HTTP, `crates/engine/src/net/child.rs:170`) → `unseal`. The broker calls `downloadRange` once per `pull`, i.e. once per 1 MiB window. Streaming a 200 MB video therefore performs ~200 IPNS resolves, ~200 head-block fetches, ~200 body unseals and ~200 floor checks for a version that cannot change mid-response — all to re-derive the same `Version` the previous window already had. This is the dominant cost on the whole feature: it is per-window network round-trips on the critical path of every buffer refill.

Cheaper: resolve the head version once when the stream opens and carry it for the life of the cursor. Either (a) add an engine-side per-stream read handle (`open_stream(node) -> handle`, `read(handle, offset, len)`) so `head_version` runs once, or (b) memoize the resolved `Version` per node for the response's lifetime behind the existing snapshot/floor gates. Option (a) also fixes findings 2 and 3 for free.

### 2. The DAG root block is re-fetched and re-decoded on every ranged read
`/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-adea2eb962539584b/crates/engine/src/content/mod.rs:215-225`

`open_content_range` starts with `read_block(... root_cid ...)` + `decode_root` unconditionally. For a full-file read that is amortized over all leaves; for the media path it is one extra HTTP round-trip **and** a CID verification per 1 MiB window — for a manifest whose contents are immutable for the version. On a 200 MB file that is ~200 redundant root fetches, and it sits directly in first-byte latency for every seek.

Cheaper: split the manifest decode out of `open_content_range` (e.g. `open_manifest(version) -> Manifest` + `open_window(&manifest, ...)`), and have the caller that already holds a stream cursor keep the decoded manifest. Same shape as finding 1's stream handle.

### 3. `MEDIA_WINDOW_BYTES` is 40 bytes larger than the production chunk size, so *every* window fetches and decrypts two leaves
`/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-adea2eb962539584b/packages/client/src/media/protocol.ts:29` (`1024 * 1024` = 1 048 576) vs `ContentProfile::PRODUCTION.chunk_size` = 1 048 536 plaintext bytes (`crates/engine/src/content/profile.rs:36`).

Because the window is strictly larger than a chunk, `leaf_range_for_byte_range` returns 2 leaves for essentially every window (window 0 → leaves 0..2, window 1 → leaves 1..3, …), and consecutive windows re-fetch the shared boundary leaf. Concrete cost: ~2 MiB of sealed blocks fetched, CID-verified and XChaCha20-unsealed to serve each 1 MiB of plaintext — roughly **2x the network bytes and 2x the AEAD work** for the whole stream, plus the discarded head/tail bytes copied out at `crates/engine/src/content/mod.rs:265`.

Cheaper: make the window chunk-aligned rather than power-of-two. Either export the plaintext chunk size across the seam and set `MEDIA_WINDOW_BYTES` to it (or a multiple), or have the broker align its cursor: read `[offset, align_up(offset+1, chunk))` for the first pull and whole chunks thereafter. Either way each window becomes exactly one leaf fetch.

### 4. `sendCapped` adds a full extra copy of every content block on the hot fetch path
`/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-adea2eb962539584b/packages/client/src/seams/http.ts:76-101`

`read_block` (`crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:281`) is the only caller and it now routes *every* root and leaf block through this path. The implementation accumulates a `Uint8Array[]` and then allocates `new Uint8Array(total)` and memcpys every chunk into it — a full 1 MiB allocation + copy per leaf, on top of the copy into wasm memory that follows. When the gateway declares a valid `content-length` (trustless gateways do for raw blocks) the destination size is already known, and when the body arrives as a single chunk the concat is pure waste.

Cheaper: if `Number.isFinite(declared)` and `declared <= maxBytes`, allocate `new Uint8Array(declared)` up front and `body.set(value, written)` directly in the read loop (still enforcing `written + value.byteLength > maxBytes` → `tooLarge`, and re-checking the final `written` against `declared`); otherwise keep the accumulate path but short-circuit `chunks.length === 1 && chunks[0].byteLength === total` to return `chunks[0]` unchanged.

### 5. Leaves inside one window are fetched strictly sequentially
`/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-adea2eb962539584b/crates/engine/src/content/mod.rs:245-267`

The `for index in leaves` loop awaits each `read_block` before starting the next. Combined with finding 3 this is 2 serialized gateway RTTs per window today, and more if the window is ever widened. Unlike the whole-file read, this latency is user-visible per buffer refill.

Cheaper: fetch the window's leaves concurrently (`futures::stream::iter(...).buffered(n)` or a bounded `join_all`), keeping the assembly order and the per-leaf length check unchanged. Peak memory stays bounded by the concurrency limit × chunk size.

### 6. No read-ahead: the pipe holds exactly one window in flight

    ['accept-ranges', 'bytes'],

  return SAFE_MEDIA_TYPES.test(mimeType) && !SVG.test(mimeType)
    ? mimeType
    : 'application/octet-stream';

function baseHeaders(mimeType: string, length: number): Array<[string, string]> {

    ['content-type', safeType(mimeType)],
    ['content-length', String(length)],
    ['accept-ranges', 'bytes'],
    ['cache-control', 'no-store'],

**1. `crates/engine/src/sync/staging.rs:212` (called from `facade.rs:1662`) — `collect_orphans` has no idle short-circuit.**

That is ≥4 IndexedDB/OPFS round-trips per poll on a device with an empty queue and an empty staging store, forever — 30 s cadence in prod, 1 s in CI. `Drain::run` (`drain.rs:426`) early-outs on an empty queue; the sweep does not, and it runs even on the ticks where the drain was skipped for missing seeds.

**2. `staging.rs:232` + `staging.rs:236` — `prune_preserved_roots` re-does I/O `orphan_staging_keys` just did.**
`orphan_staging_keys` already read the preserved-roots record (`:285`) and already fetched `staged_bytes` for every preserved root (`:302`). `prune_preserved_roots` re-reads both. Cost: `1 + P` duplicated store reads per sweep, P = preserved dead letters. Both live in the same function; the second pass could reuse the first's result.

**3. `staging.rs:276` duplicates `drain.rs:576` in the same tick.**
The drain reads and parses the whole op queue, then `collect_orphans` reads it again from the seam. Cost: one full queue enumeration + record-header re-parse per tick that the tick already paid for.

**4. `staging.rs:299-309` — queued roots are re-fetched and re-decoded every pass, unmemoized.**
For N queued uploads: N root-block reads + N CBOR `decode_root` calls + a `HashSet<Vec<u8>>` rebuilt with one allocation per leaf CID, every tick, even when the queue is byte-identical to last tick. A large file's root inlines thousands of leaf links, so this is thousands of small allocations per tick per queued upload. `QueueScanMemo` (`facade.rs:2487`) already memoizes on exactly this "queue shape" key — nothing analogous here.

**5. `staging.rs:216-219` + `staging.rs:284` — the live set is deep-cloned twice per sweep.**
`LiveBlocks::keys()` (`:196`) clones every held CID into a fresh `Vec`, then `referenced.extend(live.iter().cloned())` clones all of them again into the set. Cost: 2 full copies of O(leaves-in-flight) CIDs per sweep; passing the `Vec` by value into `orphan_staging_keys` removes one.

`LiveBlocks::record` (`:182`) bumps `generation` on every staged block, so during any in-progress write the generation guard aborts the removal loop after the full scan has already been paid for. This is precisely when staging churns most (a long upload), so every tick during a big write burns the `queued_ops` + `staged_keys` + root-expansion I/O and discards the result. A cheap up-front "any open handle → skip this pass" check would avoid the scan entirely; the sweep after the handle closes still collects.

### [HIGH] Media responses carry a caller-supplied `Content-Type` with no `nosniff`, CSP, or MIME allowlist

**Location:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-adea2eb962539584b/packages/client/src/media/range.ts:29-36`

```ts
function baseHeaders(mimeType: string, length: number): Array<[string, string]> {
  return [
    ['content-type', mimeType],
    ['content-length', String(length)],
    ['accept-ranges', 'bytes'],
    ['cache-control', 'no-store'],
  ];
}
```

**Issue:** `mimeType` flows unvalidated from `MediaSource` (`registry.ts:14`) into the `Content-Type` of a **same-origin, top-level-navigable** `/stream/<ticket>` URL. `apps/web/index.html` sets no CSP, and the SW adds no `X-Content-Type-Options`, no `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox`, and no `Content-Disposition`. The browser test only asserts the MIME round-trips (`test/browser/media.spec.ts:122`).

**Impact:** A file received through a **share** is attacker-controlled content whose name/MIME the UI will derive. `evil.html` (or `evil.svg` — SVG executes script when navigated to or framed) served as `text/html` / `image/svg+xml` on `https://app.cipherbox/` yields **XSS on the app origin**: full access to the session, the `BroadcastChannel` leader relay, and the media broker itself. This is the classic blob/SW-preview XSS and it is exactly the class of defense that belongs in the response producer, since the SW is deliberately a dumb pipe with no other guard.

**Recommendation:**
```ts

const SVG = /^image\/svg/i;

function safeType(mimeType: string): string {
  return SAFE_MEDIA_TYPES.test(mimeType) && !SVG.test(mimeType)
    ? mimeType
    : 'application/octet-stream';
}

function baseHeaders(mimeType: string, length: number): Array<[string, string]> {
  return [
    ['content-type', safeType(mimeType)],
    ['content-length', String(length)],
    ['accept-ranges', 'bytes'],
    ['cache-control', 'no-store'],
    // Vault plaintext must never execute on the app origin.
    ['x-content-type-options', 'nosniff'],
    ['content-security-policy', "default-src 'none'; sandbox"],
  ];
}
```
Add the same two headers to `unsatisfiable()` (`range.ts:38-46`). Test: assert a `text/html` and an `image/svg+xml` source are both downgraded and that `nosniff` is present on 200/206/416.

### [MEDIUM] A ranged stream can splice plaintext from two different content versions

**Location:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-adea2eb962539584b/crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2143-2163` and `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-adea2eb962539584b/packages/client/src/media/broker.ts:123-146`

) -> Result<RangedRead, EngineError> {   // { bytes, content_cid, size }

if (cursor.contentCid === null) cursor.contentCid = read.contentCid;

### What changed

Every record publish uploads its head block through the charged `POST /content/upload` ingress, so each attempt creates its own accountable pin row. A publish that failed before the record reached the transport left that row charged with nothing able to reach the block, and because the drain draws a fresh seal nonce per pass, every retry orphaned another one — for any op kind, since folder creates/deletes/renames/moves have no content CIDs at all.

The drain now notes the head CID of any publish that stopped short of the PUT fan-out (`orphaned_head`, an exhaustive match so a new error variant is a compile error) and retires the set at the end of the pass that orphaned it, independent of the op's fate. `record_orphan_head` additionally refuses any CID the live held set still names. The pending set is session-lived on the engine so a refused retire retries, and capped at `RETIRE_BATCH_MAX`.

**Key decision the issue asked for:** `PublishError::AllEndpointsFailed` deliberately does *not* orphan. It means no endpoint *acked*, not that none *stored* — retiring there would unpin the head of a record a lost ack left resolvable, turning a quota leak into an unreadable node.

**Deliberate divergence:** retirement is eager per pass rather than accumulated into the abandonment batch. It covers strictly more (an op that retries and then succeeds still orphaned rows) and needs no new staging key or format. <result># Security Review — `feat/641-sw-byte-pipe-precache`

Reviewed the working tree (nothing is committed on this branch; `git diff main...HEAD` is empty). Scope: `git diff` for the 33 modified tracked files plus all 11 untracked paths, read directly.

**No HIGH-severity findings.** No MEDIUM finding survived false-positive triage as concretely exploitable at this commit — the two candidates that looked MEDIUM (`content-type` sniffing, port hijack) are gated by facts verified below. Everything real is LOW / latent / reliability. Details, and the four "this is actually sound" verdicts the brief asked for, follow.

---

## What was verified as SOUND (asked for explicitly)

**Engine ranged read — leaf-length invariants hold, and are *stronger* than the whole-object path they replace.** `crates/engine/src/content/mod.rs:254-261` length-checks **every** fetched leaf against `chunk_size.min(manifest.size - leaf_start)` and returns `OpenError::Trust` on mismatch. Worked example proving it is load-bearing: size=40, chunk=16, request `offset=16,length=8`; a gateway serving an 8-byte leaf 1 would, *without* this check, pass the global `plaintext.len() == length` check and serve leaf-1 bytes as `plaintext[16..24]`. It is rejected. Short middle leaf, over-long final leaf, and a manifest disagreeing with the file ref's declared size (`mod.rs:226`) are all hard trust violations, not silent shifts. Clamp is against **trusted** `manifest.size` (cross-checked against `version.size`), never against fetched-block lengths. Every `saturating_*` is provably a no-op on the reachable domain — none masks a bug. Exhaustive 0..=48 × 0..=8 differential test against whole-file slicing passes.

**`sendCapped`'s memory bound is real** (`packages/client/src/seams/http.ts:57-100`). No `arrayBuffer/blob/text/json` on the capped path; the running total is checked at line 85 **before** the `chunks.push` at line 89; `await response.body?.cancel()` (line 64) fires on the declared-too-large path *before a single body byte is read*, and `await reader.cancel()` (line 86) on the streaming-overrun path; `new Uint8Array(total)` (line 93) is sized from **observed** bytes, never from `Content-Length`. Overshoot is exactly one UA read chunk (browser-set, not attacker-amplifiable). Gzip bombs are caught because the loop counts *decompressed* bytes. Header edge cases (`""`, `"-1"`, duplicate → `"100, 100"` → `NaN`, `"Infinity"`) all fall through to the streaming cap — no input skips both checks.

**Media pipe cannot buffer unboundedly *within* a stream.** `highWaterMark: 0` (`sw/pipe.ts:163`) means one 1 MiB window in flight per stream; the tab transfers the buffer rather than copying (`media/broker.ts:136`); a stalled consumer stops the pulls. The gap is *across* streams — see LOW-4.

**Range parsing, ticket entropy, precache, determinism — clean.** `media/range.ts` was executed against 26 crafted headers at `totalSize=1000` and 4 at `totalSize=0`: no case yielded `offset+length > totalSize`, a negative or `NaN` offset/length, or a wrong 416 `Content-Range`. `URL` normalization kills `/stream/../foo` and `%2e%2e` traversal, and `pipe.ts:62` gates on `url.origin === scope.location.origin`. Tickets are `crypto.randomUUID()` — 122 bits, CSPRNG, no counter, never derived from the node/CID, never logged. Precache: verified against the real `apps/web/dist/precache-manifest.json` — only `/assets/*` and `/index.html`; `resolveEntry` (`sw/precache.ts:128-138`) rejects cross-origin and `/stream/`; `CacheLike` structurally has **no `put`**; `install.ts:89-94` checks `pipe.handles()` *before* `appShellClaims`, so there is no cache-first ordering bug; `deleteStaleCaches` scopes to the `cipherbox-` prefix. Zero new `SystemTime`/`Instant::now`/`rand`/`OsRng` in engine logic. No `eval`, no dynamic `importScripts`, no `postMessage(msg, '*')`.

**`cache-control: no-store` holds on every branch that carries bytes** — `range.ts:34` and `:43` set it on 200, 206 **and** 416 via `baseHeaders`. See LOW-6 for the three body-less branches that omit it.

## LOW-1 — `/stream/` echoes an unvalidated `content-type` with no `nosniff`, and the SW serves navigations
`packages/client/src/media/range.ts:24-31`, `packages/client/src/sw/pipe.ts:62-64`, `packages/client/src/sw/install.ts:89-94`
Category: `content_type_sniffing` / stored XSS (latent). Confidence 9 on the mechanism, **2 on exploitability today**.

```ts
handles(url: URL): boolean {
  return url.origin === this.scope.location.origin && url.pathname.startsWith(STREAM_PATH_PREFIX);
}
```
No `request.mode`/`method`/`destination` guard, and `baseHeaders` emits `MediaSource.mimeType` verbatim with no `X-Content-Type-Options`. There is **no CSP anywhere** — confirmed absent from `apps/web/index.html`, `apps/web/vite.config.ts` (dev-only COOP + `Service-Worker-Allowed`), and `docker/Caddyfile` (bare `root`/`try_files`/`file_server`); no `_headers`/`netlify.toml`/`vercel.json`/nginx conf exists.

Why it is **not** MEDIUM today: `grep -rni mime crates/` returns **nothing** — the vault has no `mimeType` field, so no sharer-controlled value can reach it; and there are **zero production callers** of `createStreamUrl` (only `service.test.ts`, `registry.test.ts`, `broker.test.ts`, and the Playwright harness `test/browser/media.ts:122`). `useMediaService` is defined at `EngineProvider.tsx:97` and consumed by nothing. `blueprint/web-client.md:198-205` intends `/stream/` as a **media-element subresource**, where `text/html` does not execute.

It becomes MEDIUM the day the UI wires a real `mimeType` from file metadata *and* any navigation affordance exists (`window.open`, "open in new tab", iframe preview) — the natural next slice.

**Fix:** in `baseHeaders`, add `['x-content-type-options', 'nosniff']` and clamp `mimeType` to an `audio/*`/`video/*`/`image/*` allowlist falling back to `application/octet-stream`; in `MediaPipe.respond`, `if (request.mode === 'navigate') return new Response(null, { status: 404 })` and reject non-`GET`/`HEAD`. Cheap now, while the API has no callers to break.

## LOW-2 — SW does not validate port message shape (asymmetric with the tab side)
`packages/client/src/sw/pipe.ts:101-106`, `:94-96`, `:139`. Category: `input_validation`. Confidence 8.

```ts
const data = event.data as Partial<MediaResponse> | null;
if (typeof data?.requestId !== 'number') return;
this.sinks.get(data.requestId)?.(data as MediaResponse);
```
The tab side *does* validate (`media/broker.ts:153-174` `asRequest`, with the comment "A same-origin port is still untrusted input"); the SW side does not. Concrete effects: `chunk: 5e8` → `new Uint8Array(5e8)` throws `RangeError` **inside the sink, after `sinks.delete` and before `resolve()`**, so the `pull` promise never settles and the stream hangs; `status: 0`/`999` → `RangeError` in `respond()`; `headers` lands unvalidated in `new Headers()`. Only the port holder can send these, so it buys an attacker nothing — the realistic trigger is a version-skewed broker. Header CRLF injection is **not** possible (`new Headers` throws).

**Fix:** add an `asResponse(data)` validator in `pipe.ts` mirroring `asRequest` — discriminate on `type`, require `chunk instanceof ArrayBuffer`, `Number.isInteger(status) && 200 <= status <= 599`, `headers` an array of 2-tuples — and drop anything off-shape.

## LOW-3 — the `Some("response")` arm no longer re-checks `max_bytes` at the WASM boundary
`crates/wasm/src/seams_bridge.rs:594`. Category: `broken_invariant`. Confidence 9. **In the diff** — this PR deleted the Rust-side length check and moved the whole bound into JS.

```rust
Some("response") => http_response_from_js(result).map_err(CappedFetchError::Transport),
```
Backstopped **today** only by coincidence: the single live caller `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:281` passes `MAX_RESOLVED_RECORD_BYTES` and `read.rs:224` re-checks against *the same constant*. A second `send_capped` caller with a smaller cap silently loses the bound, and the `extern` doc at `:483-484` asserting JS is "the authoritative bound" makes that drift likely.

**Fix:** in the `"response"` arm, `if response.body.len() > max_bytes { return Err(CappedFetchError::BodyTooLarge { observed: response.body.len(), limit: max_bytes }) }`.

## LOW-4 — no cap or TTL on concurrent media streams
`packages/client/src/media/broker.ts:27, 98-103`; `packages/client/src/sw/pipe.ts:77-99`. Category: `resource_exhaustion` (in scope per the brief). Confidence 8.

Cursors are removed only on completion (`broker.ts:124`), read error (`:139`), or `cb:media:close` (`:69`); `respond()` has no in-flight counter. Honest magnitude, since the first review overstated it: with `highWaterMark: 0` the `respondWith` plumbing still issues **one** pull per abandoned fetch, so N abandoned fetches ⇒ N × 1 MiB of gateway fetch + decrypt, N × tens-of-bytes of durable tab-side `Map` entries (the 1 MiB buffer is *transferred* and sits in GC-reclaimable browser pipe memory), and GC of the dropped `Response` propagates `cancel` → `cb:media:close` → the cursor is reaped. So it is self-healing and requires an already-same-origin script holding a valid ticket. The *work* amplification is the real cost, not the map.

**Fix:** cap `this.streams.size` in `MediaBroker.open` (reply a 503 head past the cap) and give each cursor an idle TTL.

## LOW-5 — `revoke()` silently no-ops on an absolutized URL, leaving the capability live
`packages/client/src/media/registry.ts:33-36` + `packages/client/src/media/protocol.ts:59-64`. Category: `capability_lifetime`. Confidence 9.

`ticketFromPath` requires `startsWith('/stream/')`. `register` returns the relative form, but the natural caller reads it back off the element — `videoEl.src` returns `https://host/stream/<uuid>` → `null` → **silent no-op**, and the plaintext bearer capability stays resolvable. `registry.test.ts:38-45` even codifies the silent drop as intended, so a future caller gets zero feedback. A `#t=10` fragment fails identically.

Two related claims are **false** and worth correcting: `dispose()` **does** call `this.registry.clear()` (`media/service.ts:86`), and logout **does** rebuild with a fresh registry (`useAuth.ts:129` → `rebuildEngine()` → `EngineProvider.tsx:51-73` disposes and constructs a new `StreamRegistry`), so there is **no cross-account plaintext leak**. The `await this.startup` window is not exploitable — the old port is already `close()`d by `adoptPort`→`detachPort` before the stranded registry could be reached.

**Fix:** `ticketFromPath(new URL(url, self.location.origin).pathname)` (rejecting cross-origin), and return a `boolean` so a failed revoke is not silent.

## LOW-6 — `no-store` is enforced tab-side only; three SW-synthesized branches omit it
`packages/client/src/sw/pipe.ts:82` (404), `:102` (503), `packages/client/src/media/broker.ts:80-83` (404 head). Confidence 9.

The branches that carry bytes (200 **and 206**) are covered; these three ship no `cache-control` at all. Impact is limited — SW-synthesized responses aren't stored in the HTTP cache — but the guarantee currently lives entirely in `range.ts`, and `pipe.ts:94` copies `head.headers` verbatim and adds nothing, so a future broker change silently drops it.

**Fix:** in `MediaPipe.respond`, `const headers = new Headers(head.headers); headers.set('cache-control', 'no-store');` and use headers-bearing responses on the 404/503 paths, making it structurally unlosable.

## LOW-7 — zero-length chunks bypass the cap accounting
`packages/client/src/seams/http.ts:82` — `if (!value) continue;` does not catch an *empty* `Uint8Array` (`!!new Uint8Array(0) === true`). Empty chunks pass `total + 0 > maxBytes` forever and append to `chunks` without advancing `total`. Browsers don't surface empty reads from `fetch` bodies in practice, so this is theoretical. **Fix:** `if (!value || value.byteLength === 0) continue;`. (Also: the comment at `http.ts:54` claims peak is "the cap plus one chunk"; actual peak is ~2× cap during final assembly at lines 93-98, plus a third copy in wasm at `seams_bridge.rs:70` — bounded and fine at 4 MiB, but the comment is imprecise.)

## Correctness / reliability (not security — flagged because the brief asked about these seams)

- **Short read advances the cursor by the requested length** — `crates/engine/src/content/mod.rs:232` clamps to `manifest.size` and returns a possibly-shorter `Vec` with no signal; `media/broker.ts:134` does `cursor.offset = offset + length` (requested, not `chunk.byteLength`). Verified this can **only** happen at the tail of a version — never an interior window — so it is truncation, *not* misalignment: every delivered byte is CID-verified and at its correct absolute offset. Result is a body shorter than the declared `content-length` (`ERR_CONTENT_LENGTH_MISMATCH`, or a zero-byte 206). **Fix:** advance by `chunk.byteLength` and error the stream on a short read.
- **No version pinning across a stream** — `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2149-2152` calls `head_version` per window (a full IPNS fan-out + adoption gate + snapshot writeback + DAG-root fetch, **per 1 MiB**) and returns only `Vec<u8>`. Windows of one HTTP response can come from different versions. Assessed honestly: a sharer who can republish can already serve arbitrary bytes outright, and each window is individually gated and unsealed under *its own* version key, so this is not a trust escape — the realistic damage is garbled playback (including from the owner's own concurrent edit) plus hundreds of redundant resolves per video. **Fix:** capture the content CID at ticket mint and have `read_content_range` fail on a head change (the `If-Range`/ETag equivalent); this also removes the per-window resolve.
- **Single global port, last-offer-wins → the second tab breaks the first** — `sw/pipe.ts:46` holds one port; every tab brokers unconditionally at boot (`media/service.ts:109`). Tab A's ticket routes to tab B's registry → hard 404 (`broker.ts:80-83`), and `pipe.ts:95` returns it terminally (the retry loop only re-runs on `head === null`). **Strictly fail-closed** — registries are per-instance in-memory `Map`s with UUID keys, so B can never *serve* A's ticket; no cross-tab or cross-account leak. Pure availability, but two open tabs is the ordinary case. **Fix:** `Map<clientId, port>` keyed off `event.source.id`, routed by `FetchEvent.clientId`.
- **Idle body hangs forever on a port swap** — `detachPort` (`pipe.ts:196-208`) fails only requests with an *outstanding* pull; a buffered-ahead `<video>` has no sink registered, and its `pull` closure captured the now-closed port (`pipe.ts:130, 156`). No timer inside `body` (`responseTimeoutMs` is used only in `open`). Silent permanent stall, no error event. The existing test at `pipe.test.ts:292` covers exactly the complement of this gap. **Fix:** track live streams by request id, post to `this.port`, and error every live stream in `detachPort`.
- **Port-adoption authentication was assessed and rejected as a security finding.** `sw/install.ts:103-108` adopts a port from any same-origin client without checking `event.source`. Only same-origin script can reach a SW registration, `event.source` cannot distinguish XSS from the app, and the codebase *already* exposes a strictly stronger surface: `broadcast.ts:109` (`BROADCAST_CHANNEL_NAME = 'cipherbox-engine'`, a fixed name) + `leaderRelay.ts:165-184`, which answers `{kind:'download'}` from any follower with decrypted plaintext. The documented model at `broadcast.ts:60-72` is explicit: "Same origin is the trust boundary."
- **Request-id correlation across a port swap is safe, but only emergently.** No misattribution path exists — `nextRequestId` is monotonic per instance, `detachPort` removes the listener *and* closes the old port before adoption, and `broker.pump` re-checks `streams.get(requestId) !== cursor` both before and after the await. But `this.sinks` is keyed by request id alone while `body()` captures the port in a closure; there is no per-port generation tag. The LOW-2 / hung-body fix would make the invariant explicit.
