### [LOW] `MEDIA_WINDOW_BYTES` duplicates a frozen Rust wire constant in TypeScript with no parity gate

**Location:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-a2965a9e0fc546f34/packages/client/src/media/protocol.ts:26`

**Issue:** `1_048_536` is now a hand-copied mirror of `ContentProfile::PRODUCTION.chunk_size` (`crates/engine/src/content/profile.rs:36`), which the profile doc calls wire-format-frozen. Nothing fails if the two drift — the browser spec asserts against the TS constant itself (`test/browser/media.spec.ts:30`), which is self-referential. Drift is perf-only (windows straddle leaves again), never a correctness or confidentiality issue, since the reader always derives geometry from the manifest's own `chunk_size`. Still, the AGENTS.md rule-4 spirit ("TypeScript has no codec of its own") argues for the number crossing the boundary rather than being retyped.

**Recommendation:** expose `productionChunkSize()` from `crates/wasm/src/host.rs` and assert `MEDIA_WINDOW_BYTES === productionChunkSize()` in the browser suite, or at minimum add a Rust test pinning `ContentProfile::PRODUCTION.chunk_size() == 1_048_536` with a comment naming `media/protocol.ts` as the mirror.

### [INFO] `read_stream` omits the `!self.started` guard

`facade.rs:2487` — every sibling read (`read_content`, `read_content_range`, `open_content_stream`) opens with `if !self.started { return Err(NotStarted) }`. Unreachable today (a handle can only exist post-start and nothing clears `started`), but it becomes live the day a `stop()`/logout lands. Add the guard for symmetry.

### [INFO] Move residue of key material at the new pin site

`facade.rs:2477` — `Rc::new(LiveStream { version, manifest })` moves the `SecretBytes` from the stack into the `Rc` allocation. Rust does not run `Drop` on a moved-from value, so the stack copy of the 32-byte content key is left un-wiped. This is inherent to the codebase's existing `head_version() -> (Version, u64)` by-value style, not a regression in lifetime — but the diff adds one more copy site for the same key. If you ever want to close this class, the fix is to construct the `Version` in place (`Rc::new_cyclic`-style or a boxed builder), not to change zeroization.

`media/broker.ts:160` — when `isCurrent` goes false after `readStream` resolves, the up-to-1 MiB plaintext `ArrayBuffer` is dropped to the GC without a wipe. Pre-existing shape, but supersession is now more likely to race a long read. `new Uint8Array(chunk).fill(0)` on that branch matches the discipline `EngineClient.start` already applies to the login secret.

A stream holds the key and manifest but not the blocks; a prune/GC of the pinned version's leaves after a head change turns later windows into `ContentUnavailable`. Fail-closed and correct — noting it so it is not mistaken for a bug when it surfaces in the media pipe as `cb:media:error`.

## Verified clean

**Key lifetime & zeroization (Q1)**

- `cipherbox_core::suite::secret::SecretBytes` has `impl Drop { self.0.zeroize() }` and a redacted `Debug` (`crates/core/src/suite/secret.rs:36-46`); `Version` holds the content key only through it and re-redacts in its own `Debug` (`crates/core/src/seal/body.rs:195-198`). Dropping the last `Rc<LiveStream>` therefore wipes the key.
- `Rc::clone` in `read_stream` bumps a refcount — it does **not** clone `Version`, so no extra key copy is made per window. (`Version: Clone` exists but is not invoked anywhere on this path.)
- `read_stream` takes the `Rc` clone *before* the await, so a `close_stream` landing at an await keeps the pin alive and the key is wiped by the read's own drop. No path leaves a closed stream's key reachable: `close_stream` removes the only map entry, and `LiveStreams` is a plain field of `Engine`, dropped with it.
- No `RefCell` borrow is held across an await in any of the three new methods (`borrow()` is a single-statement temporary in `read_stream`; `borrow_mut()` in `open_content_stream` has no await after it). No `BorrowMutError` and no aliasing between `close_stream` and a concurrent read under the wasm `RwLock` read guards.
- WASM boundary still wraps the returned plaintext in `Zeroizing` before the copy into the JS heap (`crates/wasm/src/host.rs:420-421`), matching `download`.

**Plaintext handling (Q2)**

- `read_pinned_range` retains the full ownership story unchanged: `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>` assembly buffer, `grow_wiping` on every growth so no realloc frees a live plaintext allocation, a per-leaf `Zeroizing` chunk so trimmed head/tail bytes die at the loop, and `std::mem::take` handing terminal ownership to the caller. The split moved only the key parameter, not any ownership.
- `crates/engine/tests/content_wipe.rs` still exercises this via `open_content_range`, which now delegates into the shared body — coverage is not lost by the split.

**Trust boundary / fail-closed (Q3)**

- All four checks survive on **both** paths, because `open_content_range` now *calls* `open_content_root`: root-block CID verify (`read_block(… ContentPlane::Root)`), manifest-vs-version size cross-check, per-leaf `chunk_size`-implied length invariant, assembled-length invariant.
- Classification is byte-identical: both paths funnel through `open_read_error` / `open_dag_error` / `open_engine_error`, so Trust → `TrustViolation`, Unavailable → `ContentUnavailable`, `UnsupportedFormat` → `UnsupportedContentFormat` (`facade.rs:2766`). `UnsupportedFormat` is still not conflated with a trust verdict (#820).
- Skipping the per-window resolve does **not** drop a gate: the pinned version passed the adoption gate at open, and pinning strictly narrows what a later head change can do.
- `leaf_range_for_byte_range` clamping and its zero-`chunk_size` fail-safe are untouched; the aligned window resolves to exactly one leaf.
- The relay's capability check rejects a handle the asking follower does not own with an identical message and code in both the "unknown" and "not yours" cases — no existence oracle.
- `MediaBroker` releases the engine stream on every exit path: EOF, read error, explicit `cb:media:close`, a superseding open on the same requestId, and port teardown — including a stream whose open is still pending or rejected.
- No `downloadRange` stragglers anywhere in `packages/`, `apps/`, `crates/`.

**Encode/decode symmetry (Q4)**

- No decode-side reject was introduced; the manifest-vs-version check only moved into `open_content_root`. Its release-active encode-side counterpart is unchanged and unrepresentable-by-construction (`SealedContent`, `content/mod.rs:48-56`) with the release-firing test `a_published_version_carries_its_own_manifests_size` (`content/mod.rs:369`).
- No `debug_assert!`/`assert!` added anywhere in the diff's non-test code.

**Privacy / side channels (Q5)**

- No new logging. New error strings carry only sizes, leaf indices, and `check()` tags — no key bytes, no plaintext, no CIDs. `EngineError::UnknownStreamHandle` renders as `"unknown stream handle"` and maps to `VfsError::Internal` alongside `UnknownWriteHandle` (`crates/fuse/src/error.rs:85`).
- The BroadcastChannel now carries stream handles and plaintext `Blob`s — but it already carried plaintext `Blob`s for `download`/`downloadRange`, the channel is same-origin-only, and the token + clientId filtering is unchanged. No new trust boundary is crossed; nothing key-bearing goes on the wire (the handle is an opaque `u64`, the `RootManifest` never leaves the engine).
- The pinned `RootManifest` holds no secret: root blocks are unsealed public metadata on IPFS by design.

**Chunk alignment (Q6)**

- `1_048_536` verified equal to `ContentProfile::PRODUCTION.chunk_size` (`profile.rs:36-38`), and the doc comment's arithmetic checks out: `SEALED_LEAF_OVERHEAD = NONCE_LEN + TAG_LEN = 40`, so the *sealed* leaf is exactly 1 MiB.
- No new leakage. The gateway is already told which leaf index it is serving (the CID it is asked for), and the ordered leaf CIDs plus the plaintext size are already public in the unsealed root manifest. Alignment does not reveal structure the observer lacked; it only removes the duplicate fetch of each straddled leaf, i.e. strictly less traffic for the same information.
- Alignment holds only for playback from offset 0; a `Range` request starts mid-chunk and the reader handles arbitrary offsets correctly. Content written under a different profile (CI, or a future one) reads correctly because geometry comes from the manifest, not the constant.

**Issue:** `StreamHandle` is a per-engine counter starting at 1 (`streams.next += 1`). `EngineClient` forwards `readStream(handle, …)` to whatever `this.current` transport is *at call time*, with no epoch/token tagging. Every engine instance mints from the same small integers, and the relay's `streamOwners` map is rebuilt empty on each new leadership.

Reachable sequence (follower path):

1. Tab A (follower) opens a stream for file **Y** via leader B's relay → handle `1`, `streamOwners[1] = A`.
2. B dies; C wins the lock and spins a fresh engine + fresh relay. A's `MediaBroker` cursor for Y is idle (paused video), so nothing rejects it.
3. A opens a new stream for file **Z** via C → C's engine mints `1` again, `streamOwners[1] = A`.
4. A's stale Y cursor pulls → `readStream(1, offsetInY, …)`. Ownership check passes (A does own handle 1), and the engine serves **Z**'s pinned version at Y's offsets.

The same shape exists on the local path (leader tab demoted/re-promoted with a fresh worker). Every returned byte is CID-verified and unsealed under Z's own key, so no downstream check detects it — precisely the undetectable cross-version splice this PR exists to close, just relocated from "within one engine" to "across engines". Blast radius is same-user/same-vault (integrity, not confidentiality), but the media element renders one file's plaintext under another file's ticket URL.

**Recommendation:** tag handles with the transport generation in `EngineClient`, so the guard lives in one place and covers `WriteHandle` (which has the identical pre-existing shape — a stale `pushChunk` landing in someone else's upload):

```ts
// EngineClient
private epoch = 0;                        // ++ in installFollower() and promote()
private streamEpoch = new Map<StreamHandle, number>();

openContentStream(node: Uint8Array): Promise<StreamHandle> {
  const epoch = this.epoch;
  return this.current.openContentStream(node).then((h) => {
    this.streamEpoch.set(h, epoch);
    return h;
  });
}

readStream(handle: StreamHandle, offset: number, length: number): Promise<ArrayBuffer> {
  if (this.streamEpoch.get(handle) !== this.epoch) {
    return Promise.reject(new EngineRequestError('stream lost at a leadership swap; retry', 'unknownStreamHandle'));
  }
  return this.current.readStream(handle, offset, length);
}
```

Alternative (belt-and-braces, engine-side): mint the first handle from injected entropy at construction instead of `0`, so two engines practically never share a handle space. Cheap and it hardens the Rust API independently of the TS layer.

**Location:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-a2965a9e0fc546f34/crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1134-1137` and `:2465-2479`

```rust
const MAX_LIVE_STREAMS: usize = 32;
if streams.open.len() >= MAX_LIVE_STREAMS {
    return Err(EngineError::TooManyStreams);
}
```

**Key lifetime & zeroization (Q1)**

- `cipherbox_core::suite::secret::SecretBytes` has `impl Drop { self.0.zeroize() }` and a redacted `Debug` (`crates/core/src/suite/secret.rs:36-46`); `Version` holds the content key only through it and re-redacts in its own `Debug` (`crates/core/src/seal/body.rs:195-198`). Dropping the last `Rc<LiveStream>` therefore wipes the key.
- `Rc::clone` in `read_stream` bumps a refcount — it does **not** clone `Version`, so no extra key copy is made per window. (`Version: Clone` exists but is not invoked anywhere on this path.)
- `read_stream` takes the `Rc` clone *before* the await, so a `close_stream` landing at an await keeps the pin alive and the key is wiped by the read's own drop. No path leaves a closed stream's key reachable: `close_stream` removes the only map entry, and `LiveStreams` is a plain field of `Engine`, dropped with it.
- No `RefCell` borrow is held across an await in any of the three new methods (`borrow()` is a single-statement temporary in `read_stream`; `borrow_mut()` in `open_content_stream` has no await after it). No `BorrowMutError` and no aliasing between `close_stream` and a concurrent read under the wasm `RwLock` read guards.
- WASM boundary still wraps the returned plaintext in `Zeroizing` before the copy into the JS heap (`crates/wasm/src/host.rs:420-421`), matching `download`.

**Plaintext handling (Q2)**

- `read_pinned_range` retains the full ownership story unchanged: `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>` assembly buffer, `grow_wiping` on every growth so no realloc frees a live plaintext allocation, a per-leaf `Zeroizing` chunk so trimmed head/tail bytes die at the loop, and `std::mem::take` handing terminal ownership to the caller. The split moved only the key parameter, not any ownership.
- `crates/engine/tests/content_wipe.rs` still exercises this via `open_content_range`, which now delegates into the shared body — coverage is not lost by the split.

**Trust boundary / fail-closed (Q3)**

- All four checks survive on **both** paths, because `open_content_range` now *calls* `open_content_root`: root-block CID verify (`read_block(… ContentPlane::Root)`), manifest-vs-version size cross-check, per-leaf `chunk_size`-implied length invariant, assembled-length invariant.
- Classification is byte-identical: both paths funnel through `open_read_error` / `open_dag_error` / `open_engine_error`, so Trust → `TrustViolation`, Unavailable → `ContentUnavailable`, `UnsupportedFormat` → `UnsupportedContentFormat` (`facade.rs:2766`). `UnsupportedFormat` is still not conflated with a trust verdict (#820).
- Skipping the per-window resolve does **not** drop a gate: the pinned version passed the adoption gate at open, and pinning strictly narrows what a later head change can do.
- `leaf_range_for_byte_range` clamping and its zero-`chunk_size` fail-safe are untouched; the aligned window resolves to exactly one leaf.
- The relay's capability check rejects a handle the asking follower does not own with an identical message and code in both the "unknown" and "not yours" cases — no existence oracle.
- `MediaBroker` releases the engine stream on every exit path: EOF, read error, explicit `cb:media:close`, a superseding open on the same requestId, and port teardown — including a stream whose open is still pending or rejected.
- No `downloadRange` stragglers anywhere in `packages/`, `apps/`, `crates/`.

**Encode/decode symmetry (Q4)**

- No decode-side reject was introduced; the manifest-vs-version check only moved into `open_content_root`. Its release-active encode-side counterpart is unchanged and unrepresentable-by-construction (`SealedContent`, `content/mod.rs:48-56`) with the release-firing test `a_published_version_carries_its_own_manifests_size` (`content/mod.rs:369`).
- No `debug_assert!`/`assert!` added anywhere in the diff's non-test code.

**Privacy / side channels (Q5)**

- No new logging. New error strings carry only sizes, leaf indices, and `check()` tags — no key bytes, no plaintext, no CIDs. `EngineError::UnknownStreamHandle` renders as `"unknown stream handle"` and maps to `VfsError::Internal` alongside `UnknownWriteHandle` (`crates/fuse/src/error.rs:85`).
- The BroadcastChannel now carries stream handles and plaintext `Blob`s — but it already carried plaintext `Blob`s for `download`/`downloadRange`, the channel is same-origin-only, and the token + clientId filtering is unchanged. No new trust boundary is crossed; nothing key-bearing goes on the wire (the handle is an opaque `u64`, the `RootManifest` never leaves the engine).
- The pinned `RootManifest` holds no secret: root blocks are unsealed public metadata on IPFS by design.

**Chunk alignment (Q6)**

- `1_048_536` verified equal to `ContentProfile::PRODUCTION.chunk_size` (`profile.rs:36-38`), and the doc comment's arithmetic checks out: `SEALED_LEAF_OVERHEAD = NONCE_LEN + TAG_LEN = 40`, so the *sealed* leaf is exactly 1 MiB.
- No new leakage. The gateway is already told which leaf index it is serving (the CID it is asked for), and the ordered leaf CIDs plus the plaintext size are already public in the unsealed root manifest. Alignment does not reveal structure the observer lacked; it only removes the duplicate fetch of each straddled leaf, i.e. strictly less traffic for the same information.
- Alignment holds only for playback from offset 0; a `Range` request starts mid-chunk and the reader handles arbitrary offsets correctly. Content written under a different profile (CI, or a future one) reads correctly because geometry comes from the manifest, not the constant.

# CipherBox - AI Agent Instructions

## Project Context

CipherBox is a privacy-first, zero-knowledge E2EE personal cloud storage system on IPFS/IPNS. The repo is mid-rewrite: **v2 is being built on `main`** against the blueprint corpus below; v1 is frozen on branch `v1` (tag `v1-freeze`) and receives no changes.

## Documentation Structure

The normative source of truth for the v2 build:

| Document                  | Purpose                                                       |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CONTEXT.md`              | The v2 ubiquitous language — use these terms, exactly         |
| `blueprint/core.md`       | `crates/core` — wire formats, crypto, KDF catalog, KAT regime |
| `blueprint/engine.md`     | `crates/engine` — the one stateful brain, seam traits, gates  |
| `blueprint/api.md`        | API residual surface, registry, mailbox, republisher          |
| `blueprint/web-client.md` | WASM hosting, tab leadership, `packages/client`, `apps/web`   |
| `blueprint/desktop.md`    | FS projection, host adapters, Tauri shell                     |
| `blueprint/testing.md`    | Suite map, CI gates, coverage policy                          |
| `blueprint/deploy.md`     | Freeze mechanics, release management, staging pipeline        |

The as-built v1 spec corpus, ADRs, and all design-decision history live in [FSM1/cipher-box-next](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next) (wayfinder map issue 1 indexes every decision). The `docs/` folder is v1 legacy — being rewritten during the build; trust `blueprint/` when they conflict.

## Terminology Standards

Use the v2 ubiquitous language defined in `CONTEXT.md` — every domain term (scope, epoch, ascent link, grant blob, adoption gate, floor law, eager set, …) has exactly one name there. General conventions: `publicKey`/`privateKey`/`ipnsName`/`ipnsRecord` spelled out in full camelCase for API fields, snake_case for database columns.

## Critical Security Rules

1. **Never** store `privateKey` or any seed in localStorage/sessionStorage
2. **Never** log sensitive keys or seeds
3. **Never** send unencrypted keys to the server — the server is zero-knowledge and NEVER sees plaintext or unencrypted keys
4. **All crypto lives in `crates/core`** — TypeScript has no codec or crypto of its own; never implement crypto in TS
5. Primitives are fixed by `blueprint/core.md`: XChaCha20-Poly1305 sealing, BLAKE3 tree KDF, X25519 + HPKE key wrapping, REDACTED signing — no key derives outside the frozen KDF edge catalog
6. Every resolved record passes the adoption gate; a failure is a fail-closed trust violation, never mere staleness
7. Clear sensitive material from memory after use (zeroize at the terminal owner only — a callee must not zero caller-owned buffers)
8. **Encode/decode fail-closed symmetry** — when a decode/verify path hard-rejects an invariant violation (a trust/malformed check), the matching encode/produce path MUST enforce the same invariant with a **release-active** check that returns `Err` — never `debug_assert!`/`assert!`, which are stripped in release. Otherwise a release build can sign and publish bytes its own decoder always rejects (an unopenable ledger/commitment/body). Keep these encode-side checks consistent with the `crates/core/src/seal/body.rs` `assert_children_unique` convention, and cover them with a test that fires in a release build.

## API Contract and Clients

There are **no generated API clients** and no codegen loop. The engine contains the single hand-written Rust API client; the NestJS API's OpenAPI document is a committed docs artifact, not a build input. The contract is enforced by the live contract-test suite (the sdk-e2e descendant) running the real client against a real API instance on every PR — see `blueprint/testing.md`.

## Code Generation Guidelines

1. All engine, codec, and crypto logic is Rust (`crates/core`, `crates/engine`); TypeScript exists only in `packages/client` (WASM wrapper, browser seams) and `apps/web` (React UI)
2. Use `Uint8Array`/`Vec<u8>` for binary data, not strings
3. Determinism is injected: entropy, time, and policy enter as parameters/seam traits — never call clocks or RNGs directly in core/engine logic
4. Every suite must block a merge in a named CI gate the day it lands (`blueprint/testing.md` law 1); assert behavior, never source text

## Code Style

### Comments

Comments explain _why_, not _what_, and stay short. **If you need a paragraph-long comment to justify why a workaround is OK, the code is wrong — fix the code.** A long apologia for a hack is a smell: rework the code so it no longer needs defending, rather than documenting the shortcut. Reserve multi-line comments for genuinely non-obvious domain rationale — a spec citation, a cryptographic invariant, a wire-format or fail-closed constraint — not for excusing a shortcut.

Two recurring shapes of this smell go beyond excusing a hack — avoid both:

- **Absence-justifying comments** — prose explaining why a path that is _not_ in the code does not happen (e.g. "`replay()` does not run here, so `decode_queue` is the only source at this stage"). It bloats the diff and rots into a falsehood the moment that path is wired — a stale in-code claim that actively misleads. Describe what the present code does; a bare cross-reference suffices if a reader must know a related path lives elsewhere.
- **Unchanged-code apologia** — a doc block defending code this change does not modify (e.g. why a parameter stays a raw borrow, on a function the diff leaves untouched). It is scope creep into untouched code and reads as pre-emptive defensiveness. Leave that rationale where it already lives.

State genuine non-obvious domain rationale **once**, at its home (the type or definition), not restated on every caller. These cost real review cycles — `/simplify`, CodeRabbit, and Greptile all flag them.

Length discipline for the permitted domain-rationale exception: state each invariant **once** and prefer a one-line cross-reference to the blueprint / `CONTEXT.md` over re-deriving it in prose. Do not narrate the happy path — the code is the narrative, and a comment restating what the next lines plainly do rots out of sync and misleads. A module header past ~25 lines is almost always restating the spec: keep only the rationale that is non-obvious _from the code itself_ and cite the blueprint for the rest.

## Architecture Pillars

- **Auth:** Web3Auth key derivation; challenge-signature login; short-lived JWT + rotating refresh
- **Storage:** IPFS content, IPNS metadata — the network is canonical; clients verify records cryptographically; CipherBox infra (Kubo, someguy) is accelerator-only and the API never serves records
- **Keys:** seeded per-scope derivation with key-regression epochs; rotation = O(1) root cut + lazy wave (`CONTEXT.md`)
- **One Rust core:** desktop links it natively, web loads it as WASM in a worker; one implementation, one KAT set
- **Sync:** pull-only focus-window polling, cache-first, offline op queue; no push in v2.0 (seam ready)
- **Desktop:** Tauri + FUSE mount (FUSE-T SMB on macOS, libfuse3 on Linux, WinFsp on Windows)
- **No TEE:** the republisher is a keyless re-PUT module inside the API; client-signed 90-day EOLs

## Out of Scope

- Billing/payments, mobile apps, real-time collaborative editing, team accounts
- Vault import (cut in v2), client-side search (deferred, designed-for)
- Executing anything against the frozen `v1` branch

## Verification with MCP Tools

### Puppeteer MCP Verification (REQUIRED)

**ALWAYS attempt to verify application changes using Puppeteer MCP** when it is available. This ensures implemented features work correctly at runtime.

**When to use Puppeteer MCP:**

- After implementing UI components
- After modifying styles or layouts
- After adding new pages or routes
- After any user-facing changes

**Verification workflow:** the dev server runs at `http://localhost:5173`. Navigate, screenshot, assert the elements and computed styles the change touches, then exercise the interaction. Element waits go through `puppeteer_evaluate` polling — there is no dedicated wait tool.

**If Puppeteer MCP is not available:**

- Document what needs human verification
- Provide manual test steps
- Flag items in VERIFICATION.md

### Pencil Design Files

Pencil design files exist at `designs/*.pen` (with `designs/DESIGN.md`) but are not actively maintained right now. `.pen` files are encrypted: read them only through the Pencil MCP tools — never `Read` or `grep` them directly.

## Git Workflow

### Branch Protection Rules

- **NEVER push directly to `main` branch** - all changes must go through feature branches and PRs
- Create feature branches with descriptive names (e.g., `feat/add-auth`, `fix/ipns-publish`)
- All commits should be made on feature branches first
- Merge to main only via pull requests

### Branch Naming

- `feat/` - New features
- `fix/` - Bug fixes
- `docs/` - Documentation updates
- `refactor/` - Code refactoring
- `chore/` - Maintenance tasks

### Commit Messages

Commits must follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format:

```text
type(optional-scope): description

[optional body]
```

Valid types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`. Any scope string is allowed (e.g., `feat(api): add health endpoint`). A custom commitlint rule additionally rejects parenthesized text in the subject line (it breaks Release Please parsing).

Enforcement: commitlint is configured via `commitlint.config.js`, and PR titles are validated in CI by `.github/workflows/pr-title.yml`. <result>Altitude review of the #972 diff (`fix/972-follower-read-port`). No correctness hunting; verdict plus depth findings, ordered by weight.

## Verdict

The core layering call is right. Making the private port a **generic `PortCourier` seam** rather than teaching `BroadcastTransport`/`LeaderRelay` about `navigator.serviceWorker` is the correct depth: the courier knows nothing about reads, leadership, or vault semantics, the leadership-bound handshake stays in the transport pair, and the SW stays a stateless forwarder. `LeaderRelay` adopting per-follower ports next to `writeOwners`/`focus` (all reclaimed by the same `cb:bye`) is the right home. Three-method seam, all three used, no speculative generality — not over-generalized.

The problems are all *placement and size*, plus one real cross-module coupling.

## Findings

**1. `/apps/web/src/providers/EngineProvider.tsx:58` (+ `packages/client/src/portCourier.ts:138`) — Service Worker registration has two unrelated owners, and follower reads now depend on the optional one's side effect.**
`ServiceWorkerCourier.worker()` only awaits `container.ready`; nobody in the engine path ever calls `register()`. The only registrar is `MediaService.begin()`, which by design swallows registration failure ("streaming is an enhancement: a failure degrades the tab, never its boot"). After this change, that swallowed failure silently kills *every follower read*, not just streaming — and the ordering (`createEngineClient` before `createMediaService(client).start()`) is an accident of provider code, not a stated dependency. `apps/web` is untouched in the diff, so nothing records the new edge.
Deeper change: one `ServiceWorkerHost` in `packages/client` owning `register`/`ready`/`controller`/message routing, consumed by both `MediaService` and `ServiceWorkerCourier`, and passed to `EngineClient` as an explicit constructor edge. Failing that, at minimum have `defaultCourier()` take the registration promise, so "no SW ⇒ reads fail closed" is a declared contract rather than a race.

**2. `packages/client/src/broadcastTransport.ts:44,143-248` — a second protocol state machine now lives inside the correlation transport.**
Six new fields (`portPromise`, `releasePort`, `portGeneration`, `hostWaiters`, `adoptionWaiters`, `portWaits`) and seven methods implement rendezvous → connect → hello → adoption → generation fencing, interleaved with the existing leadership state machine. The class's stated job is "correlate requests over the channel"; it now also owns a brokerage protocol.
Deeper change: extract a `LeaderReadPort` collaborator (in-file, mirroring the existing `FocusRegistry`-in-`leaderRelay.ts` precedent, or a peer module) constructed with `(channel, clientId, courier, isActiveLeader)`, exposing `acquire(): Promise<MessagePortLike>`, `onLeaderMessage(msg)`, `reset(error)`, `close()`. `BroadcastTransport` then keeps only token/gate concerns and three one-line delegations.

**3. `packages/client/src/broadcastTransport.ts:44,145` — `OPEN_GATE` is the smell marker: a special case beside the shared base rather than a generalization of it.**
`CorrelatedTransport.request(readyGate, send)` exists precisely so a subclass supplies its readiness gate; `read()` instead awaits `ensurePort()` *outside* `request` and passes a sentinel resolved promise, which also moves the base's `terminalError` short-circuit after the brokerage await.
Deeper change: widen the shared skeleton to `request<T, G>(gate: Promise<G>, send: (id: number, gate: G) => void)` and call `this.request<T, MessagePortLike>(this.ensurePort(), (id, port) => port.postMessage(...))`. `OPEN_GATE` disappears and the no-hang ordering is restored for reads.

**4. `packages/client/src/portCourier.ts:12-25` — the SW wire protocol lives inside a tab-side implementation module, inverting the repo's own protocol/impl split.**
`sw/install.ts` imports `RELAY_*`/`RelayMessage` from `portCourier.ts`, a module that also defines `ServiceWorkerCourier` and constructs `MessageChannel`. The established convention is `media/protocol.ts` (shared wire) ↔ `media/service.ts` (tab) ↔ `sw/pipe.ts` (worker).
Deeper change: split a `src/relay/protocol.ts` (constants + `RelayMessage` + `MessagePortLike`) from the courier implementation, and have both the SW and the tab import the protocol only.

**5. `packages/client/src/broadcastTransport.ts:31`, `leaderRelay.ts:26`, `portCourier.ts:9` — `MessagePortLike` is now a general transport type imported from `media/protocol.js` by four non-media modules.**
It was media-specific when it was written; it isn't any more.
Deeper change: move it to the neutral relay/port protocol module from finding 4 and let `media/protocol.ts` re-export or import it.

**6. `packages/client/src/sw/install.ts:133-173` — the forwarder is at the right *level* (stateless, in the worker, `waitUntil`-extended) but in the wrong *file*.**
`install.ts` is otherwise pure wiring; `MediaPipe` is a class in `pipe.ts`. The relay adds a three-branch message router plus a free `deliverPort` helper directly in the installer, and reaches into `pipe.ts` for `WindowClientLike`.
Deeper change: a small `sw/relay.ts` (`PortRelay` with `handles(data)` / `deliver(...)`, injectable like `deps.pipe`), leaving `install.ts` a router.

**7. `packages/client/src/sw/pipe.ts:19-30` — shared SW types were widened to `unknown` to accommodate a second consumer instead of being lifted out.**
`WindowClientLike.postMessage` went from typed `MediaPortRequest` to `unknown`, and `ClientsLike.matchAll` grew `includeUncontrolled` — both driven by the relay, yet both still live in the media pipe module. That is a typed wire traded for a generic one, mitigated only by a call-site `const ask: MediaPortRequest`.
Deeper change: move `WindowClientLike`/`ClientsLike` to a shared `sw/clients.ts` and type `postMessage` as `MediaPortRequest | RelayMessage`, keeping the worker's outbound wire statically checked.

**8. `packages/client/src/broadcast.ts` `cb:portWanted`/`cb:portHost` — the four-step handshake may be one step deeper than the problem.**
The follower asks for an address, the leader publishes one (a forgeable message needing its own token check and its own waiter set), then the follower connects and says hello, then the leader stamps ready. Inverting it — the follower puts *its own* courier address on `cb:hello`/`cb:portWanted`, the leader `connect()`s to it and stamps `cb:portReady` — removes the `cb:portHost` message type, the `hostWaiters` set, and the forged-host surface entirely, at equal cost elsewhere. Not a defect in the current shape; flagging it as the place where the remaining complexity concentrates, worth one deliberate think before it ossifies as wire.

**9. `packages/client/test/browser/leadership.ts:119` — a 200×50ms poll for `navigator.serviceWorker.controller` is scaffolding-grade.**
Deeper change: race `navigator.serviceWorker.ready` against a `controllerchange` listener; the poll is a 10-second worst case in a merge-blocking suite.

**10. `blueprint/web-client.md:205-220` — the SW now has three responsibilities, documented in two disjoint places.**
The followers bullet (line ~101) carries the new brokerage role, but the SW's own section still enumerates only "dumb byte pipe" and "precaches the app shell". One line there ("and brokers a private port between two tabs, reading neither") keeps the SW's contract stated where a reader looks for it.</result>

Production serves the SPA with `try_files {path} /index.html` (`docker/Caddyfile:18`) and the deploy wipes the web root (`rm: true`, `.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml:460`). A redeploy landing mid-`install` makes `cache.addAll` (`precache.ts:52`) receive `200 text/html` for a now-missing hashed asset and cache the shell HTML under a `.js` URL. `resolveEntry` validates the URL, never the response.

## Scope of impact — stated precisely

**Online users self-heal.** `respondFromAppShell` handles navigations network-first (`precache.ts:111-112`), so a returning user gets the new `index.html`, whose new hashed asset URLs are not in `precached`, fail `appShellClaims` (`:91`), and pass through to the network.

The real impact is a stale offline shell plus unbounded cache growth across deploys. This is an integrity and correctness defect, not a live exploitation path. Recording that explicitly because an earlier draft of this finding overstated it as a permanent white-screen, which is wrong.

## Fix direction

- Stamp a build id into the worker via `define` on the nested `build()` at `apps/web/vite.config.ts:43-58`, and key `APP_SHELL_CACHE` off it, so both the update check and the rotation follow the build.
- Optionally carve `/assets/*` out of the Caddy SPA fallback so a missing asset 404s and `addAll` rejects rather than caching HTML under a `.js` URL.

Production serves the SPA with `try_files {path} /index.html` (`docker/Caddyfile:18`) and the deploy wipes the web root (`rm: true`, `.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml:460`). A redeploy landing mid-`install` makes `cache.addAll` (`precache.ts:52`) receive `200 text/html` for a now-missing hashed asset and cache the shell HTML under a `.js` URL. `resolveEntry` validates the URL, never the response.

## Scope of impact — stated precisely

**Online users self-heal.** `respondFromAppShell` handles navigations network-first (`precache.ts:111-112`), so a returning user gets the new `index.html`, whose new hashed asset URLs are not in `precached`, fail `appShellClaims` (`:91`), and pass through to the network.

The real impact is a stale offline shell plus unbounded cache growth across deploys. This is an integrity and correctness defect, not a live exploitation path. Recording that explicitly because an earlier draft of this finding overstated it as a permanent white-screen, which is wrong.

## Fix direction

- Stamp a build id into the worker via `define` on the nested `build()` at `apps/web/vite.config.ts:43-58`, and key `APP_SHELL_CACHE` off it, so both the update check and the rotation follow the build.
- Optionally carve `/assets/*` out of the Caddy SPA fallback so a missing asset 404s and `addAll` rejects rather than caching HTML under a `.js` URL.

# CipherBox - AI Agent Instructions

## Project Context

CipherBox is a privacy-first, zero-knowledge E2EE personal cloud storage system on IPFS/IPNS. The repo is mid-rewrite: **v2 is being built on `main`** against the blueprint corpus below; v1 is frozen on branch `v1` (tag `v1-freeze`) and receives no changes.

## Documentation Structure

The normative source of truth for the v2 build:

| Document                  | Purpose                                                       |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CONTEXT.md`              | The v2 ubiquitous language — use these terms, exactly         |
| `blueprint/core.md`       | `crates/core` — wire formats, crypto, KDF catalog, KAT regime |
| `blueprint/engine.md`     | `crates/engine` — the one stateful brain, seam traits, gates  |
| `blueprint/api.md`        | API residual surface, registry, mailbox, republisher          |
| `blueprint/web-client.md` | WASM hosting, tab leadership, `packages/client`, `apps/web`   |
| `blueprint/desktop.md`    | FS projection, host adapters, Tauri shell                     |
| `blueprint/testing.md`    | Suite map, CI gates, coverage policy                          |
| `blueprint/deploy.md`     | Freeze mechanics, release management, staging pipeline        |

The as-built v1 spec corpus, ADRs, and all design-decision history live in [FSM1/cipher-box-next](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next) (wayfinder map issue 1 indexes every decision). The `docs/` folder is v1 legacy — being rewritten during the build; trust `blueprint/` when they conflict.

## Terminology Standards

Use the v2 ubiquitous language defined in `CONTEXT.md` — every domain term (scope, epoch, ascent link, grant blob, adoption gate, floor law, eager set, …) has exactly one name there. General conventions: `publicKey`/`privateKey`/`ipnsName`/`ipnsRecord` spelled out in full camelCase for API fields, snake_case for database columns.

## Critical Security Rules

1. **Never** store `privateKey` or any seed in localStorage/sessionStorage
2. **Never** log sensitive keys or seeds
3. **Never** send unencrypted keys to the server — the server is zero-knowledge and NEVER sees plaintext or unencrypted keys
4. **All crypto lives in `crates/core`** — TypeScript has no codec or crypto of its own; never implement crypto in TS
5. Primitives are fixed by `blueprint/core.md`: XChaCha20-Poly1305 sealing, BLAKE3 tree KDF, X25519 + HPKE key wrapping, REDACTED signing — no key derives outside the frozen KDF edge catalog
6. Every resolved record passes the adoption gate; a failure is a fail-closed trust violation, never mere staleness
7. Clear sensitive material from memory after use (zeroize at the terminal owner only — a callee must not zero caller-owned buffers)
8. **Encode/decode fail-closed symmetry** — when a decode/verify path hard-rejects an invariant violation (a trust/malformed check), the matching encode/produce path MUST enforce the same invariant with a **release-active** check that returns `Err` — never `debug_assert!`/`assert!`, which are stripped in release. Otherwise a release build can sign and publish bytes its own decoder always rejects (an unopenable ledger/commitment/body). Keep these encode-side checks consistent with the `crates/core/src/seal/body.rs` `assert_children_unique` convention, and cover them with a test that fires in a release build.

## API Contract and Clients

There are **no generated API clients** and no codegen loop. The engine contains the single hand-written Rust API client; the NestJS API's OpenAPI document is a committed docs artifact, not a build input. The contract is enforced by the live contract-test suite (the sdk-e2e descendant) running the real client against a real API instance on every PR — see `blueprint/testing.md`.

## Code Generation Guidelines

1. All engine, codec, and crypto logic is Rust (`crates/core`, `crates/engine`); TypeScript exists only in `packages/client` (WASM wrapper, browser seams) and `apps/web` (React UI)
2. Use `Uint8Array`/`Vec<u8>` for binary data, not strings
3. Determinism is injected: entropy, time, and policy enter as parameters/seam traits — never call clocks or RNGs directly in core/engine logic
4. Every suite must block a merge in a named CI gate the day it lands (`blueprint/testing.md` law 1); assert behavior, never source text

## Code Style

### Comments

Comments explain _why_, not _what_, and stay short. **If you need a paragraph-long comment to justify why a workaround is OK, the code is wrong — fix the code.** A long apologia for a hack is a smell: rework the code so it no longer needs defending, rather than documenting the shortcut. Reserve multi-line comments for genuinely non-obvious domain rationale — a spec citation, a cryptographic invariant, a wire-format or fail-closed constraint — not for excusing a shortcut.

Two recurring shapes of this smell go beyond excusing a hack — avoid both:

- **Absence-justifying comments** — prose explaining why a path that is _not_ in the code does not happen (e.g. "`replay()` does not run here, so `decode_queue` is the only source at this stage"). It bloats the diff and rots into a falsehood the moment that path is wired — a stale in-code claim that actively misleads. Describe what the present code does; a bare cross-reference suffices if a reader must know a related path lives elsewhere.
- **Unchanged-code apologia** — a doc block defending code this change does not modify (e.g. why a parameter stays a raw borrow, on a function the diff leaves untouched). It is scope creep into untouched code and reads as pre-emptive defensiveness. Leave that rationale where it already lives.

State genuine non-obvious domain rationale **once**, at its home (the type or definition), not restated on every caller. These cost real review cycles — `/simplify`, CodeRabbit, and Greptile all flag them.

Length discipline for the permitted domain-rationale exception: state each invariant **once** and prefer a one-line cross-reference to the blueprint / `CONTEXT.md` over re-deriving it in prose. Do not narrate the happy path — the code is the narrative, and a comment restating what the next lines plainly do rots out of sync and misleads. A module header past ~25 lines is almost always restating the spec: keep only the rationale that is non-obvious _from the code itself_ and cite the blueprint for the rest.

## Architecture Pillars

- **Auth:** Web3Auth key derivation; challenge-signature login; short-lived JWT + rotating refresh
- **Storage:** IPFS content, IPNS metadata — the network is canonical; clients verify records cryptographically; CipherBox infra (Kubo, someguy) is accelerator-only and the API never serves records
- **Keys:** seeded per-scope derivation with key-regression epochs; rotation = O(1) root cut + lazy wave (`CONTEXT.md`)
- **One Rust core:** desktop links it natively, web loads it as WASM in a worker; one implementation, one KAT set
- **Sync:** pull-only focus-window polling, cache-first, offline op queue; no push in v2.0 (seam ready)
- **Desktop:** Tauri + FUSE mount (FUSE-T SMB on macOS, libfuse3 on Linux, WinFsp on Windows)
- **No TEE:** the republisher is a keyless re-PUT module inside the API; client-signed 90-day EOLs

## Out of Scope

- Billing/payments, mobile apps, real-time collaborative editing, team accounts
- Vault import (cut in v2), client-side search (deferred, designed-for)
- Executing anything against the frozen `v1` branch

## Verification with MCP Tools

### Puppeteer MCP Verification (REQUIRED)

**ALWAYS attempt to verify application changes using Puppeteer MCP** when it is available. This ensures implemented features work correctly at runtime.

**When to use Puppeteer MCP:**

- After implementing UI components
- After modifying styles or layouts
- After adding new pages or routes
- After any user-facing changes

**Verification workflow:** the dev server runs at `http://localhost:5173`. Navigate, screenshot, assert the elements and computed styles the change touches, then exercise the interaction. Element waits go through `puppeteer_evaluate` polling — there is no dedicated wait tool.

**If Puppeteer MCP is not available:**

- Document what needs human verification
- Provide manual test steps
- Flag items in VERIFICATION.md

### Pencil Design Files

Pencil design files exist at `designs/*.pen` (with `designs/DESIGN.md`) but are not actively maintained right now. `.pen` files are encrypted: read them only through the Pencil MCP tools — never `Read` or `grep` them directly.

## Git Workflow

### Branch Protection Rules

- **NEVER push directly to `main` branch** - all changes must go through feature branches and PRs
- Create feature branches with descriptive names (e.g., `feat/add-auth`, `fix/ipns-publish`)
- All commits should be made on feature branches first
- Merge to main only via pull requests

### Branch Naming

- `feat/` - New features
- `fix/` - Bug fixes
- `docs/` - Documentation updates
- `refactor/` - Code refactoring
- `chore/` - Maintenance tasks

### Commit Messages

Commits must follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format:

```text
type(optional-scope): description

[optional body]
```

Valid types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`. Any scope string is allowed (e.g., `feat(api): add health endpoint`). A custom commitlint rule additionally rejects parenthesized text in the subject line (it breaks Release Please parsing).

Enforcement: commitlint is configured via `commitlint.config.js`, and PR titles are validated in CI by `.github/workflows/pr-title.yml`. Note that the husky `commit-msg` hook was replaced by an Entire CLI wrapper and currently does not run commitlint locally — follow the format regardless, since CI will reject non-conforming PR titles.

### Mandatory PR Review Flow

Every code PR runs these review gates after it is opened as a **draft**, before it is driven toward merge — mandatory, not optional:

1. `/simplify` — tighten the diff: remove speculative generality, dead abstraction, and duplication.
2. `/security-review` — trust boundaries, fail-closed behavior, auth/expiry gates, injection, DoS/resource exhaustion, concurrency, and determinism seams.
3. `/crypto-privacy-review` — **required whenever the diff touches crypto**: `crates/core` primitives, key/seal material, or trust-boundary and fail-closed reads.

Run each on the PR's own diff (`git diff main...HEAD`) and fold real findings back into the code and tests before requesting a CodeRabbit/Greptile review. If a slash-command skill is unavailable in your environment, do a rigorous manual pass against that review's checklist instead — never skip a gate. Self-review is the floor, not the ceiling: layer an independent reviewer pass on crypto- and trust-critical PRs. A pure documentation change with no code surface is exempt.

### Releases & Versioning

See the `releases` skill (`.claude/skills/releases/SKILL.md`) for the v2 release scheme, version surfaces, staging tag pipeline, and the v1 freeze. Normative source: `blueprint/deploy.md`.

The two halves of #974's fix direction happen to live in separate PRs: the build-id cache key in **#979**, the `/assets/*` fallback carve-out already in **#969**. `Closes #974` on #979 stays correct once both merge, and no follow-up issue is needed. I've noted that on #979 so its "deliberately left out" paragraph doesn't read as missing scope.

Two things I got wrong that are worth flagging plainly:

1. I described #969 as "declarative headers, safe to merge without a slot" from its line count alone. It contains a routing change that decides whether a request 404s or returns the SPA shell. Reading the diff before advising would have caught that — the same care I applied to #964's agent report, which I didn't apply to my own recommendation.
2. I proposed folding work that was already done, on the strength of an agent's "left out" note rather than checking the target PR.

Separately: `git worktree list` shows **21 worktrees**, many for already-merged branches — `feat/641`, `feat/869`, `chore/965`, `feat/920`, `fix/921`, `feat/917`, `feat/910`, `feat/805`. input.command: git worktree list --porcelain | grep '^branch refs/heads/' | sed 's|^branch refs/heads/||' | grep -v '^worktree-agent-' > /tmp/branches.txt; cat /tmp/branches.txt

## What changed (30 files, +886/−142)

**Engine core**
- `crates/engine/src/content/mod.rs` — split `open_content_range` into `open_content_root` (fetch + CID-verify the root, cross-check `manifest.size` vs `version.size`) and `read_pinned_range` (leaves); the old function is now their composition, so both paths run provably identical checks. `read_pinned_range` takes `&Version` (not a bare key) and re-asserts the manifest/version pairing per window; both are `pub(crate)`.
- `crates/engine/src/facade.rs` — `StreamHandle`, `LiveStream`/`LiveStreams`, `streams` field, `open_content_stream`/`read_stream`/`close_stream`, extracted `project_head` (shared with `read_content_range`, kept *after* the read so a fail-closed reject folds nothing), `EngineError::UnknownStreamHandle`.
- `crates/wasm/src/host.rs` — `openContentStream`/`readStream`/`closeStream` replace `downloadRange`; `readStream` now rejects non-integral offsets/lengths, not just non-finite ones.
- `crates/fuse/src/error.rs:85`, `crates/engine/src/lib.rs:63` — new variant/export.

**TypeScript seams** — `worker/protocol.ts`, `worker/serve.ts`, `worker/engineHost.ts`, `worker/engineWasm.ts`, `transport.ts`, `correlatedTransport.ts`, `broadcast.ts` (a `cb:stream` axis), `broadcastTransport.ts`, `leaderRelay.ts`, `engineClient.ts`, `facade.ts`, `testkit.ts`, `media/broker.ts`, `media/protocol.ts`, `index.ts`.

## Two things worth flagging

1. **The review passes found a HIGH that defeated the fix.** `StreamHandle` is a per-engine counter restarting at 1, so a handle carried across a leadership swap named a *different* node's live stream on the next engine — the same undetectable splice, one layer up. `EngineClient` now mints its own monotonic handle over the engine's and drops the table on every transport swap. Covered by `engineClient.test.ts` "refuses a stream handle minted by a leadership that has been replaced", verified red first (`expected 1n not to be 1n`).
2. **`MEDIA_WINDOW_BYTES` 1 MiB → 1,048,536** — one production chunk exactly. The round 1 MiB sat 40 bytes past every chunk boundary and fetched two leaves per window.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --all --check` | clean, exit 0 |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | `Finished dev profile` — no errors/warnings |

| `cargo check -p cipherbox-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` | `Finished dev profile` |
| `cargo test -p cipherbox-engine` | 13 suites ok; lib `584 passed; 0 failed`, `write_plane` 74 passed |

| `packages/client` playwright `media.spec.ts` | `8 passed (2.4s)` |

**Red-before-green, verified by simulating the pre-fix behavior:** `a_stream_serves_the_pinned_version_across_a_head_change` assembled window 0 from version A and every later window from B; `a_stream_pays_one_resolve_and_one_root_fetch_for_the_whole_body` counted 39 gateway fetches instead of 13.

## Deliberately left out (all in #981)

- **No admission cap or idle eviction on `LiveStreams`.** The write plane is bounded by the staging ledger; the read plane isn't. Choosing the cap and its refusal verdict is a design call the issue doesn't cover.
- **A dead Service Worker port still strands its cursor and pin** — `MessagePort` has no close event, so the tab-side broker isn't told. I did fix the adjacent leaks (drop before the 404/416 early returns, release on every pump exit, lazy open so an abandoned request costs nothing).
- **`MEDIA_WINDOW_BYTES` remains a hand-mirrored Rust constant** with no parity gate. Binding it across the wasm seam needs a new public binding plus plumbing through `MediaService`.

`Engine::read_content_range` stays public as the one-shot read behind `read_content` — three review agents flagged it as now having only one production caller; I kept it rather than churn the #641 integration test that covers its clamping semantics.

<result>## /security-review — PR #972 (follower read port), branch `fix/972-follower-read-port`

---

### (a) NEW exposure introduced by this diff

**MEDIUM — the follower processes `cb:portResult` on a port it has *not* adopted, bypassing the token gate the same function implements**
`/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-abf0602d090c3f392/packages/client/src/broadcastTransport.ts:214-233` (specifically 226-229)

`awaitReady()` binds one listener that does both jobs: it gates `cb:portReady` on `fromActiveLeader(token)` (correct), but then falls through and handles `cb:portResult` **unconditionally, on every offered port**, calling `this.settle(...)` into `CorrelatedTransport`'s shared pending map.

Attack: the follower broadcasts `cb:portWanted{clientId, address}` on the origin-wide channel, so any same-origin context learns the address the instant the rendezvous opens. It calls `courier.connect(address)` and immediately posts `{type:'cb:portResult', requestId: N, ok:true, result: <forged>}`. Those messages are queued before the follower calls `port.start?.()` (line 232), so they are delivered in the same task the port arrives — the attacker does not have to win the adoption race, and never has to produce a token at all. `settle()` resolves whatever pending id matches. The pending map is shared with commands and writes, so this settles in-flight `cb:command` acks and `commitWrite` op-ids as well as reads, with attacker-chosen values (a forged `SnapshotDescriptor` or a forged plaintext `ArrayBuffer` reaches the UI).

This is integrity, not confidentiality — but it defeats the only gate the diff implements, and it contradicts both the code comment at line 156-158 ("a port counts only once it opens with the active leadership's token") and `blueprint/web-client.md:24` ("A follower takes only a port that greets it with the active leadership token").

Fix: split the listener. Bind only a greeting listener up front; attach the `cb:portResult` handler inside `adopt`/`take`, or guard the result branch on `port === <the adopted port>`. One-line-ish, and it makes the existing test ("takes no read port from a context that is not the active leader") actually meaningful — that test only asserts the impostor is *sent* nothing; it never has the impostor send a `cb:portResult`. Add that case.

---

**MEDIUM — a superseded port can be adopted, wedging every subsequent read forever (no attacker required)**
`/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-abf0602d090c3f392/packages/client/src/broadcastTransport.ts:160-211` and `/Users/.../packages/client/src/leaderRelay.ts:196-216`

Nothing correlates a delivered port with the brokerage that asked for it. The leader keys `readPorts` by `clientId` and calls `detachPort(clientId)` (leaderRelay.ts:210) on every `cb:portWanted`, so "last portWanted wins" on the leader while "first valid greeting wins" on the follower (`take()`, broadcastTransport.ts:178-189). Two concrete non-adversarial sequences:

1. Brokerage #1 times out at `portTimeoutMs` (SW cold start / slow first `whoami` round-trip) → `portPromise` cleared → next read starts brokerage #2 and posts a second `cb:portWanted`. The leader's *first* `connect` resolves, registers, and greets; brokerage #2 adopts that port (token valid, generation unchanged). The leader then processes `cb:portWanted` #2 and `detachPort` **closes the port the follower just adopted**.
2. Two brokerages genuinely run concurrently: `abortBrokerage` is only armed *after* `courier.address()` resolves (lines 164-203), so a `dropPort()` during the SW address round-trip cannot cancel attempt #1; it nulls `portPromise`, and `onLeader` (line 327) immediately starts attempt #2. Both have live `onPort` subscriptions and the courier fans every delivered port to both — so either brokerage may adopt either port, and `finish()` in one clobbers `this.abortBrokerage`/`this.releasePort` of the other (leaked port).

Failure mode either way: the follower holds a resolved `portPromise` for a dead port. `port.postMessage` on it silently drops, there is **no read timeout, no close detection, and nothing to settle the pending entry** — every subsequent read hangs forever while commands keep working, so the UI looks alive. This violates the explicit no-hang contract stated at broadcastTransport.ts:7-10 and correlatedTransport.ts:4-6.

Same wedge is reachable adversarially with one broadcast message: `cb:portWanted{clientId: <victim's, read off the channel>, address: <attacker's>}` makes the leader close the victim tab's live read port.

Fix: carry a per-brokerage nonce in `cb:portWanted`, echo it in `cb:portReady`, and adopt only the matching nonce; on the leader, key/replace `readPorts` on that nonce (and don't detach the old entry until the new port is greeted). Independently, give port reads a terminal settlement path — reject pending reads when the port is dropped and/or a per-read deadline — so no read can outlive its wire.

---

**LOW/MEDIUM — unbounded, unauthenticated `readPorts` growth on the leader (and SW work per message)**
`/Users/.../packages/client/src/leaderRelay.ts:95, 146-155, 196-216`

`cb:portWanted` is accepted from anyone, with an attacker-chosen `clientId` and `address`, and each one costs the leader a `MessageChannel` + an SW `matchAll` scan (`sw/relay.ts:14`), and adds a `ReadPortEntry` (port + bound listener) that is only ever removed by a matching `cb:bye`, a re-broker under the *same* clientId, or leader teardown. A same-origin script can grow that map without limit with distinct clientIds; entries whose delivery failed (`deliverPort` closed the port because the target was gone) are dead on arrival and never reaped. Benignly, a follower tab that is closed or crashes sends no `cb:bye` and mints a fresh `clientId` on reload, so the map grows across a long-lived leadership.

`FocusRegistry.perClient` already has the same unbounded-by-clientId shape (pre-existing), but these entries pin ports and listeners. Fix: cap/expire entries (e.g. reap on failed `postPort`, or bound the map and evict LRU), and consider requiring a prior `cb:hello` for that clientId before dialing.

Related, bounded, LOW: during a brokerage the follower's `offers` set (broadcastTransport.ts:172) accepts unlimited ports for the whole `portTimeoutMs` window, binding a listener per port; all are closed at `finish()`.

---

**LOW — `close()` does not stop a brokerage that has not yet armed `abortBrokerage`**
`/Users/.../packages/client/src/broadcastTransport.ts:236-243, 257-271`

If the transport is closed (including the promote-to-leader path, `engineClient.ts:234`) while `brokerPort()` is still inside `courier.address()`, `abortBrokerage` is null, so the closed transport still posts `cb:portWanted` on the shared channel and holds an `onPort` subscription for up to `portTimeoutMs`. The generation fence catches the adoption (port released, promise rejected), so this is self-healing — but a just-promoted tab makes its own relay open, register, and then strand a `readPorts` entry keyed by its own clientId. Fix: check `this.closed`/`terminalError` at the top of the executor in `brokerPort`, and arm `abortBrokerage` before the async prefix.

---

**LOW (accepted by the issue's threat model, but new in shape) — the adoption gate is a race the attacker wins by being fast**
`/Users/.../packages/client/src/broadcastTransport.ts:217-224`, token minted at `/Users/.../packages/client/src/leaderRelay.ts:101`, broadcast on every `cb:leader`

The leadership token is broadcast in the clear on the origin-wide channel, so an impostor can replay it in a `cb:portReady`. If its port arrives before the real leader's, `take()` adopts it and **closes the real leader's port** as a losing offer — the attacker then serves every read (forged results) and learns exactly which nodes the follower reads. #972 explicitly accepts that the token does not authenticate against an active attacker, so I am not re-litigating it; noting only that the diff's comments read as if it does.

Cheap hardening if you want the race gone: invert the dial direction — have the leader publish *its* courier address on the `cb:leader` beacon and have the follower `connect` to it. The SW then delivers the port to the client id the follower already believes is the leader, which no third context can intercept. It reduces the attack surface to the pre-existing "forge a `cb:leader` beacon" path rather than adding a new independent one, and it deletes the `portWanted`/`portReady` handshake (and with it findings 1 and 2's root cause). Note this also removes the incidental broadcast of every follower's SW client id — currently an otherwise-unenumerable capability handle (only the SW can `matchAll`) that the channel now publishes origin-wide, letting any context push ports at any tab that ever brokered.

---

### (b) PRE-EXISTING, unchanged by this diff (noted, not re-litigated)

- **The leader authenticates nobody.** `openReadPort` dials any address named in `cb:portWanted` and then serves any `cb:portRead` on that port (leaderRelay.ts:196-226). An active same-origin attacker still gets plaintext on demand — exactly as it could by posting `cb:read` on main and reading the broadcast `cb:response`. The diff closes *passive* eavesdropping only, which is the stated goal.
- **`cb:leader` beacons are unauthenticated** (broadcastTransport.ts:315-328): any context can install its own token, then forge acks/events. The token has always been integrity-defence-in-depth, not authentication.
- **Per-client destructive messages keyed by an unauthenticated `clientId`** (`cb:bye` → `releaseWrites` + now `detachPort`; `cb:focus` → focus union): pre-existing pattern; the diff adds `detachPort` to it (see finding 2).
- **No cap on concurrent reads or on `downloadRange` length** — an attacker-driven `cb:portRead` storm hits the engine unthrottled, same as `cb:read` did.

### (c) Non-issues / verified clean

- **Fail-closed, no silent fallback.** The `cb:read` case is gone from `LeaderRelay.receive` entirely (`rg` confirms zero remaining references outside tests), so there is no broadcast path left to fall back onto. Missing SW → `unavailableCourier` / a 5 s `ready` deadline (`portCourier.ts:118-131`) → reads reject. `openReadPort` returns silently on a failed `connect` and the follower fails on its own gate. `defaultCourier()` only returns a live courier when `navigator.serviceWorker` exists.
- **Untrusted-input shape checks are present** where they matter: `cb:portWanted` validates `clientId`/`address` are strings (leaderRelay.ts:151); `onPortMessage` requires `type === 'cb:portRead'` and a numeric `requestId`; an unknown `read.kind` falls through `readValue` to `undefined` and a throw inside it is caught by `serveRead`'s try. SW `RELAY_DELIVER` closes the port when `to` is not a string (`sw/install.ts:141-144`) and `deliverPort` closes it when the target client is gone. `RELAY_WHOAMI` tells a client only its own id.
- **Buffer ownership / zeroization is correct.** The transferred `ArrayBuffer` originates in the worker, is transferred into the leader (`worker/serve.ts:82` `postOwned`, `engineHost.ts:42-46` `ownedBuffer`) and is not aliased or cached anywhere in the leader, so transferring it out at `leaderRelay.ts:232-236` detaches a buffer the leader solely owns — terminal-owner rule respected, no callee zeroing a caller's buffer. Transferring is strictly better than the old `Blob` clone: the plaintext leaves the leader's heap.
- **Nothing logs or persists plaintext or key material.** No new `console.*`, no storage writes; the `collectBytes` hex walker is test-only and is the assertion itself.
- **Determinism seams unchanged** — no clock/RNG introduced beyond the pre-existing `crypto.randomUUID()` token; both timeouts are injectable (`CourierOptions.timeoutMs`, `BroadcastTransportOptions.portTimeoutMs`). Minor nit: `portTimeoutMs` is not plumbed through `EngineClientConfig`, only `courier` is.
- **Availability note, not a defect:** followers in contexts without a Service Worker (SW disabled, insecure origin) now mirror nothing at all. That is the blueprint's stated intent (`blueprint/web-client.md:24-26`).

**Recommended before merge:** fix finding 1 (adopt-gate bypass) and finding 2 (nonce-correlate the brokerage + settle reads when the port dies). Findings 3-5 are reasonable follow-ups; if you take the dial-direction inversion, it subsumes 1, 2, and 5.</result>

# Crypto / Privacy Review — `fix/972-follower-read-port`

**Verdict:** the confidentiality goal of the diff is met — vault plaintext, snapshot descriptors and SIWE nonces genuinely leave the origin-wide `BroadcastChannel`, the Service Worker genuinely never observes either end of the read port, and nothing plaintext-bearing is persisted. But the diff **removes an authentication check that the wire it replaces had**: the follower accepts `cb:portResult` from any same-origin port that has not presented the leadership token, and that settles pending *commands and writes*, not just reads. That is a concrete regression against the exact threat the existing `token` machinery was built for. Two comments and one blueprint passage also claim more than the code delivers.

## NEW findings (introduced by this diff)

### [HIGH] Unauthenticated port injects forged results into any pending request

**Location:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-abf0602d090c3f392/packages/client/src/broadcastTransport.ts:214-233`

```ts
private awaitReady(port: MessagePortLike, adopt: (release: () => void) => void): void {
  const listener = (event: MessageEvent): void => {
    const message = event.data as ReadPortResponse | { type?: unknown };
    if (message.type === 'cb:portReady') {
      ...
      if (!this.fromActiveLeader(token)) return;   // gated
      ...
    }
    if (message.type !== 'cb:portResult') return;
    const result = message as Extract<ReadPortResponse, { type: 'cb:portResult' }>;
    if (result.ok) this.settle(result.requestId, true, undefined, result.result);  // NOT gated
    else this.settle(result.requestId, false, result.error, undefined, result.code);
  };
  port.addEventListener('message', listener);
  port.start?.();
}
```

**Issue:** the listener is bound (and `start()`ed) on **every** offered port, before adoption, and the `cb:portResult` branch carries no token check and no "is this the adopted port" check. `brokerPort` publishes `cb:portWanted{clientId, address}` on the shared channel (`broadcastTransport.ts:204-208`), and `deliverPort` (`/…/packages/client/src/sw/relay.ts:23-24`) will hand a port to that address for *any* same-origin caller. `CorrelatedTransport` uses one `pending` map and one small monotonic `nextId` for commands, writes and reads (`/…/packages/client/src/correlatedTransport.ts:59-61,108-109`), so a sprayed `requestId 1..N` hits whatever is in flight. The old wire gated the equivalent path: `receive()` still checks `fromActiveLeader(response.token)` before settling (`broadcastTransport.ts:291-300`), and there is a dedicated test for it (P1-4). The port path lost that.

The window is attacker-controlled, not incidental: the leadership token is broadcast in the clear on `cb:leader`, so any same-origin context can post a valid `cb:leaderGone` (`broadcastTransport.ts:330-339`), forcing `dropPort` + re-broker on demand, then race the rendezvous.

**Proven:** a throwaway vitest against the real `BroadcastTransport`/`LeaderRelay`/`FakeCourierNetwork` — a `manualRefresh` command whose engine never answers resolved as `ok` after an impostor courier dialed `'f'` and posted `{type:'cb:portResult', requestId:1, ok:true}` with **no token at all**.

**Impact:** a same-origin context forges success/failure of writes and commands (e.g. `commitWrite` resolving with an attacker-chosen op id, a failed `create` reported as success), and can hand forged snapshot/plaintext results to reads issued on a port it wins. Same-origin is the declared trust boundary (`leaderRelay.ts:98-101`), so this is defence-in-depth — but it is defence-in-depth this codebase deliberately implements everywhere else, and the diff silently drops it.

**Recommendation:** bind the result branch only after the greeting validates — the port becomes the capability, the token only gates entry:

```ts
private awaitReady(port: MessagePortLike, adopt: (release: () => void) => void): void {
  const results = (event: MessageEvent): void => {
    const message = event.data as ReadPortResponse | { type?: unknown };
    if (message.type !== 'cb:portResult') return;
    const result = message as Extract<ReadPortResponse, { type: 'cb:portResult' }>;
    if (result.ok) this.settle(result.requestId, true, undefined, result.result);
    else this.settle(result.requestId, false, result.error, undefined, result.code);
  };
  const greet = (event: MessageEvent): void => {
    const message = event.data as { type?: unknown; token?: unknown };
    if (message.type !== 'cb:portReady' || typeof message.token !== 'string') return;
    if (!this.fromActiveLeader(message.token)) return;
    port.removeEventListener('message', greet);
    port.addEventListener('message', results);
    adopt(() => { port.removeEventListener('message', results); port.close(); });
  };
  port.addEventListener('message', greet);
  port.start?.();
}
```

Add the regression test in the shape I used (impostor posts `cb:portResult` with **no** token while a command is in flight; assert the command stays pending).

### [MEDIUM] A detached read port strands the read forever — breaks the documented no-hang contract

**Location:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-abf0602d090c3f392/packages/client/src/leaderRelay.ts:164-170` (`cb:bye` → `detachPort`) and `/…/packages/client/src/broadcastTransport.ts:138-142` (`read` has no deadline)

**Issue:** the leader now tears down a follower's read port on `cb:bye`, an unauthenticated broadcast message carrying only a `clientId`. A `MessagePort` whose peer closed fires no event, `postMessage` on it silently no-ops, and `request()` has no per-request timeout — the follower only rejects pending work on a leadership change (`onLeader`/`onLeaderGone`) or `close()`. Under a *live, unchanged* leadership the read never settles.

**Proven:** with an adopted, working port, a third context posting `{type:'cb:bye', clientId:'f'}` left the follower's next `snapshot(null)` unsettled indefinitely.

This directly contradicts `broadcastTransport.ts:7-10` ("a torn-down or leader-dead transport **rejects** every pending request, never hangs") and the same claim in `correlatedTransport.ts:4-6`. It is reachable without an attacker too — any silent loss of the port (SW/port teardown, a stale `cb:bye` from a reused clientId) produces a permanently spinning UI rather than a retry.

**Recommendation:** give the read path liveness of its own: a per-read deadline that calls `dropPort` (which must then also `rejectPending` for reads bound to that port) and lets the next read re-broker. Belt and braces: on the leader, only `detachPort(clientId)` when a *replacement* port for that client is adopted, and drop the `cb:bye` teardown of read ports (the write-handle release there is a separate, pre-existing decision).

### [MEDIUM] `leaderRelay.ts:12-14` claims "No plaintext rides the channel" — it does

### What was built

Follower read results (`snapshot`, `siweChallenge`, `download`, `downloadRange`) no longer ride the origin-wide `cipherbox-engine` `BroadcastChannel`. The follower asks where this leadership takes ports (`cb:portWanted` → `cb:portHost`), dials it through the Service Worker, names itself (`cb:portHello`), and adopts the port once the leader greets with the active leadership token. Reads then flow `cb:portRead`/`cb:portResult` over that port, with `ArrayBuffer` results **transferred**, not wrapped in a `Blob`.

A `BroadcastChannel` carries no transferables, so a Service Worker is the only cross-tab route for a `MessagePort`. The worker is a stateless forwarder — it names a client back to itself and forwards the far end of a `MessageChannel`, reading neither.

The follower asks where this leadership takes ports (`cb:portWanted` → `cb:portHost`), dials it through the Service Worker, names itself (`cb:portHello`), and adopts the port once the leader greets with the active leadership token. Reads then flow `cb:portRead`/`cb:portResult` over that port, with `ArrayBuffer` results **transferred**, not wrapped in a `Blob`.

A `BroadcastChannel` carries no transferables, so a Service Worker is the only cross-tab route for a `MessagePort`. The worker is a stateless forwarder — it names a client back to itself and forwards the far end of a `MessageChannel`, reading neither.

input.content:
Identified while building #972 and deliberately left out of that PR, which scoped itself to follower read **results**.

## The gap

#972 moves `snapshot`, `siweChallenge`, `download`, and `downloadRange` results off the origin-wide `cipherbox-engine` `BroadcastChannel` and onto a per-follower `MessagePort`. The write direction was not moved.

`pushChunk` still rides the channel as a `Blob` handle, so upload plaintext is delivered to every same-origin context — every other tab, iframe, and worker on the origin — which then discards it. Command arguments travel the same way: filenames, contact codes, and the `siweLogin` signature.

The asymmetry is now the notable part. After #972 a follower's reads are private to the leader and unreadable by a bystanding context, while its uploads are not. Anyone reasoning about the channel from the read path will draw the wrong conclusion about the write path.

## Threat model, stated honestly

Same as #972's: exploiting this requires script execution on the origin, and such a script already has more direct routes. This is defence-in-depth and blast-radius reduction, not a new privilege boundary. It matters because the channel is the wrong instrument for carrying plaintext, and #972 has already built the right one.

## Why it is cheap now

The port, its handshake, its adoption gate, and the transfer path all exist after #972. `pushChunk` becomes a transfer over the established port rather than a `Blob` on the bus — the expensive part of the work is already paid for.

## Scope

- Route `pushChunk` payloads over the per-follower `MessagePort`, transferring the buffer rather than wrapping it.
- Move value-bearing command arguments off the channel by the same route.
- Extend the existing coverage: the second same-origin context in `leadership.spec.ts` must observe **no** upload plaintext and no command arguments while a follower writes, exactly as it already asserts for reads.

Part of #655

1. Informational: "I have kicked off the coderabbit review on #951 since a lot has changed since the last review and there were over 20 comments on that PR, so definitely worth another review in my books."

5. "re the review path i just merged #967 without a coderabbit review as i felt it was simple enough not to burn a slot on it"
